articleTitle: Measuring Line Parameters of Multiconductor Cables using a Vector Impedance Meter
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In the present paper, a method to measure the parameters of a multiconductor transmission line is given. The method is accurate, straightforward and only needs a single vector impedance meter or equivalent. The method has been applied for frequencies in a range from 20 kHz up to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: Characterisation by Time-Frequency Analysis of the EM Disturbances Produced by Railway Substations
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper aims to propose a methodology to characterize the electromagnetic disturbances which are provided by the railway substations which supply the railway electrical infrastructure. Currents measurements were performed inside a substation in order to identify the harmonics and the transient signals which are created by the power devices of the substation. Finally, this paper suggests exploiting a time- frequency analysis to automatically detect transient signals.

articleTitle: Characterisation of a New Joining Structure for Application to Shielding Boxes Made of Conductive Plastics
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: When using shielding boxes made of conductive plastics, the main problem is how to contact both parts of the box in a conductive way. A new low-cost joining structure has been developed and characterised. Both the joining structure as the characterisation method and procedure are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Lightweight, Multilayer, Shielding Textile Materials with a High Capability to Absorb Electromagnetic Radiation within the Range of High Frequency
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper concerns multilayer, shielding textile-polymeric materials with a high shielding effectiveness. This effectiveness results first of all from their high capability to absorb electromagnetic radiation (EMR) brought about to a large extent by the intensification of multiple internal reflections at the boundaries between the layers of component materials. These new shielding materials are characterised by low thicknesses and surface weights, amounting to 1.0 - 2.0 mm and 90 - 400 g/m<sup>2</sup>, respectively, depending on their structures. Such materials with various structures, containing various functional particles, meet high requirements of EMR shielding effectiveness within the frequency range tested from 8.0 to 18.0 GHz. Their coefficient of EMR absorption is at a level of ≥40%, and in some structures it even exceeds 70%, while the reflection coefficient is ≤20% and that of transmission amounts to ≤40%, approaching even 1%.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Waveguide Cell for Measurement of the Shielding Effectiveness of Anisotropic Materials
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A method for measuring the shielding effectiveness of planar anisotropic materials using a rectangular waveguide cell is proposed. Computational models are used to verify the behaviour of the cell and validate its ability to measure shielding effectiveness. Results of measurements on a control sample and three carbon-fibre composite laminates in a GTEM cell are presented. A dynamic range of 70 dB with a capability to discriminate 20 dB of anisotropy is achieved in the frequency range 400-1600 MHz using cubic cells of side length 200 mm and 300 mm.

articleTitle: Intelligent Mains Radiofrequency Interference Filters
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A soft- and hardware application to control frequency response of radiofrequency interference network filters is proposed. The main requirements of radiofrequency interference filters are examined. Experimental researches of filter's frequency response using modern software are implemented. A microcontroller unit for efficient change of frequency response is analyzed.

articleTitle: Interaction of Low Frequency Magnetic Fields with Car Chassis
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The subject of this paper is numerical modeling of car chassis made of thin highly conductive and magnetic materials and exposed by low frequency magnetic fields. Incorporating reduction of thickness of sheet into Maxwell equations leads to approximate boundary conditions, written for normal components of magnetic fields of free space. These magnetic fields are radiated by single and double layer magnetic charges, located on the interface surface. Resulting equations are solved via Method of Moments. Numerical simulations are compared with measurement data for plane sheets made of different materials. Excellent agreement is found in all considered cases. Computations of magnetic fields, radiated from supply cable in the car illustrate capabilities of the method.

articleTitle: A Measurement Method to Determine the Reflection Coefficient of a Sommerfeld's Single-Wire Wave DUT
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: An improved one-port calibration method for determining the reflection coefficient of a Sommerfeld's singlewire wave DUT (Device under Test) is investigated. The unknown reflection coefficient of the Short-Open-Load (SOL) calibration standards is deduced by using the slotted line method. As an application of this technique, an absorber (a mixture of ferrite tiles and foam absorbers) and an absorbing clamp are used as DUT, whose reflection coefficient is measured twice: first using the slotted line method and then with the new calibration method. At the end, a comparison between the both results is presented.

articleTitle: Bayesian Networks Modeling in System-Level Susceptibility Assessments for Intentional EMI
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The intentional electromagnetic interferences (IEMI) pose dangerous threats to the electronic systems, especially the civilian infrastructures. In the system-level susceptibility or vulnerability investigations, it is very necessary to build an appropriate mathematical model. From the standpoint of the reliability engineering, the Bayesian networks (BN) is introduced to analyze and assess the functional safety of the complex systems. As the crucial step in the application, the BN model is built based on the philosophy of the electromagnetic topology (EMT) and the fault tree analysis (FTA). It can not only represent the interactions of the systems with IEMI, but also conduct the dependability analysis. The detailed modeling processes are presented. The advantages and disadvantages of the three tools, BN, EMT and FTA, are compared and commented, and the further research needed to be done is proposed finally.

articleTitle: An Effective and Low-Cost Measurement System for EMC Pre-Compliance Testing of Radiated emissions in the Range 2-8 GHz
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The pre-compliance measurement of radiated emissions from printed circuit boards (PCBs) is here addressed. In particular an effective and low-cost measurement system is described for pre-compliance radiated emission tests in the range 2-8 GHz and under far field conditions. The goal is to propose an original test system through which estimating the effectiveness of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design solutions at PCB level. To this aim, a detailed description of the system is provided and an analisys of the system test repeatability given. In particular, a 0.5 dB repeatability level is assessed for devices under test having maximum dimension not larger than nearly 20 cm. Some practical case studies are finally presented, proving the effectiveness of the system after the adoption of some well-known EMC techniques at PCB level.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Complementary Split Ring Resonators and Electromagnetic Band-Gap as EMI Reduction Structures
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this work a comparison between complementary split ring resonators (CSRRs) and Electromagnetic Band-Gaps (EBGs) in terms of EMI filter performance is developed. Results show a similar EMI rejection level in both cases but CSRRs present a significantly better signal integrity response. A good agreement between simulations and experimental results is achieved.

articleTitle: Far-Field and Near-Field Analysis of Shielding Effectiveness of Slotted Enclosure at Frequencies Below 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Shielding Effectiveness (SE) calculated for metal slotted enclosure, obtained using three different software suites (FEKO [1], WIPL-D [2] and COMSOL [3]) is presented. For the SE analysis the electromagnetic field in both near as well as far region is considered. The effect of the spatial radiation pattern of an enclosed radiator on the results of SE calculations has been taken into account using the Poynting (S) vector integration and compared with other common methods of SE analysis. The FEKO, WIPL-D and COMSOL outputs were found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Simulating Lightning Tests to Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The risk of destruction due to lightning makes simulating the effects of lightning strikes a necessity. We modeled a radar enclosure and simulated the effect of a lightning strike. The results have been validated using full threat lightning current tests.

articleTitle: High Frequency Calibration of the 41 Inch (1.04 m) Receiving Monopole with and Without Connecting Counterpoises and with Different Sources
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The 41 inch (1.04 m) monopole antenna is used from 10 kHz to 30 MHz at a distance of 1m from the Equipment Under Test (EUT) and its associated cables and so the antenna is invariably used in the near field. Many commercially available 1.04m monopoles are not calibrated but rely on a purely theoretical far field value based on antenna and buffer input capacitances. This paper shows that the antenna factor measured in the near field is different from that predicted for the far field and depends on the source of radiation (monopole or transmission line). Also the antenna factor of the receiving monopole and the E field incident on it, from a standard source of radiation, both change when the counterpoise of the monopole is either isolated from ground, connected to a ground plane on a table or to an underlying floor ground plane. Even more so when no counterpoise is used.

articleTitle: A Statistical Approach to Radiated Immunity Testing of Digital Hardware in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The statistical characteristics of re-radiated spectra of a simulated digital equipment-under-test under radio frequency interference in a reverberation chamber are studied. Statistical models of linear coupling and reradiating channels in a reverberating environment together with nonlinearities of the equipment scattering properties are synthesized into an overall analytical model of the overall probability distribution. The fit between theoretical predictions and measurement results is verified. This technique allows tracking of the statistics of re-radiated spectra and comparison between results under different RF interference levels. It may be possible to utilize these statistics for new diagnostic tools based on reverberation test standards e.g. IEC 61000-4-21.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Electromagnetic Interference of a WAVE Inter-Vehicle Communication System on Vehicle Electronics
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Inter-vehicle communication systems present an increasing popularity due to their critical, for public safety, as much as attractive and convenient applications. This technological tendency could potentially become hazardous for automotive electronics. The radiated immunity of automotive electronics in electromagnetic fields caused by inter-vehicle communication systems described by the IEEE 802.11p WAVE standard or its equivalents is studied in this paper. The electric field produced in critical points of the interior of a vehicle is estimated by means of full wave Finite Difference Time Domain method simulations. In each simulation, the vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure communication according to the characteristics of the IEEE WAVE standard is assumed.

articleTitle: Simulation of Noise Voltage Impulses after Switching Processes in Automotive Wiring Harnesses using a SPICE Model
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Electromechanical relays are still irreplaceable for switching operations of high-current load devices. This ranges from small switching relays for automotive applications to large contactors for jointing whole feeder branches in the main grid. In any case an extreme change of the resistance occurs in the relays switched circuit. This process is often accompanied by electric sparks or even electric arc ignitions, which may lead to impulses of high amplitude and short rise times. This induces broadband and high-frequency noise voltages, which spread on the respective wiring network. Modeling this problem in the field of automotive applications using SPICE serves here as an excellent example for EMC relevant phenomena.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of UWB Antennas for Body Area Network (BAN) Applications using a Highly Accurate CAD Model of the Human Body
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A CAD model of human body is generated from magnetic resonance images (MRI) by a segmentation procedure. This model is used to predict the communication performances of ultra wideband (UWB) antennas for body area network (BAN) in different scenarios by an electromagnetic field numerical tool. The transmitting UWB antenna is considered to be on (wearable) and in (implanted) the human body, while the receiving UWB antenna is placed in air and faced to the transmitting antenna. The path-loss is computed assuming different tilt positions of the transmitting antenna and separation distances between antennas.

articleTitle: Theoretical Considerations about the Determination of Statistically Independent Stirrer Position of Mode-Stirred Chambers
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes a possibility to simulate correlated boundary conditions inside a reverberation chamber and to analyze them regarding their autocorrelation function. Therefore a modified numerical plane wave representation is used. An important result is that the classical 1 / e-criterion overestimates the number of independent tuner positions by a factor of 2.5 to 3. Moreover the autocorrelation function varies heavily between simulations with same parameters and so the number of independent tuner positions as well. This effect is also known from measurements. With suitable averaging it can be shown that the number of independent tuner positions does not depend on the measurand (received power, field strength, transmission line current). If not only one measurand, but a whole distribution is used to analyze the tuner efficiency, then the fluctuation range decreases and the reliability of approximating the independent tuner positions increases significantly.

articleTitle: Procedure to Calculate the Inductance of a Circular Loop Near a Metal Plate
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes the influence of metallic objects on the inductance as a function of the separation distance. We focus our attention on the benchmark configuration of a circular loop antenna near an infinite conducting plate. We consider the quasi-static approach, thus with a constant current distribution over the entire loop. The results are obtained by numerical integration and the accuracy of the numerical integration procedure is verified for a circular loop antenna in free space, for which a closed analytical solution exists. The results are particularly interesting in the domain of low frequency and high frequency Radio Frequency IDentification, where mutual influence of multiple reader antennas is often suppressed by means of a metallic shielding, which results in an important decrease of the readout distance and a detuning of every reader antenna.

articleTitle: Spatial Distribution of Shielding Effectiveness Inside Lightning Protection System in the Case of Nearby Stroke
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents a numerical analysis of spatial distribution of electromagnetic (EM) field shielding effectiveness of grid-like spatial shields for the case of a nearby lightning strike. The electric and magnetic field attenuation characteristics for different types of lightning protection systems (LPS) are investigated. Differences between shielding effectiveness of electric and magnetic fields are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Higher Harmonics Contents in Supply Voltages in Big Trade Building
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The analysis of higher harmonics content in supply voltages in a big trade building has been presented in this paper. In the considerations the results of measurements of phase voltages (measured in supply point of analyzed trade building) have been used. The measurements were carried out in three phases during one week, simultaneously. The main electrical receivers in such a type of the building are discharge light sources (fluorescent lamps). The statistical tools have been also used in the analysis.

articleTitle: Estimation of Whole-Body Averaged SAR of Grounded Human at Resonance Frequency from Ankle Current of Simplified Phantom
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The purpose of the present study is to discuss the feasibility of a simple physical phantom for estimating whole- body averaged specific absorption rate (SAR) in humans grounded on the perfect conductor at their respective resonance frequencies. The motivation of this investigation is that whole- body averaged SAR at resonance frequencies for exposure at the reference level is close to the basic restriction. However, it is difficult to conduct SAR measurement in practical environment. Thus, we propose a scheme to estimate whole-body averaged SAR of humans in terms of measured ankle current of a simplified phantom. This scheme utilizes an analogy of human bodies and a quarter-wavelength monopole antenna at their resonance frequencies. The effectiveness of our proposal has been verified by comparing with the ankle currents of the realistic human model and equivalent phantom.

articleTitle: The Effect of Rician Statistics on the Measurement of Shielding Effectiveness of Enclosures in Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Reverberation chamber measurements for EMC testing rely on the condition that the field intensity is uniform inside the chamber. This paper details the case where this condition may not be met and the effects that this has on the measurement of the Shielding Effectiveness of electrically large physically small enclosures according to the proposed upgrade of IEEE Std. 299. The Rician K-factor is presented as a way of determining stirring effectiveness of the reverberation chamber. A simulation of the distributions that occur with the addition of Rician components is carried out, and experiments are undertaken to determine the effect on the Shielding Effectiveness of the enclosures under test. It is seen that the Shielding Effectiveness measurement is dependent on maintaining control of the K-factor.

articleTitle: Maximum and Average Field Strength in Enclosed Environments
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Electromagnetic fields in large enclosed environments are reflected many times and cannot be predicted anymore using conventional models. The common approach is to compare such environments with highly-reflecting reverberation chambers. The average field strength can easily be predicted using the central limit theorem. The maximum field strength is, in theory, nearly impossible to predict. Actual environments are however not perfect, and the maximum field strength is bound to a maximum. A ray-tracing model has been developed to predict the maximum field for actual (lossy) environments and measurements in a reverberation chamber has been carried out.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of VHF-LISN Specified to Radiated Emission Test in Proficiency Testing Program
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The inter-laboratory comparison as the proficiency testing program based on the ISO/IEC Guide 43-1 have been periodically performed to the EMI test laboratories in Japan by VLAC (Voluntary EMC Laboratory Accreditation Center Inc.), which is the Japanese Accreditation Body of EMC testing laboratories. Lor the evaluation of technical ability of the radiated emission measurement, the artifact in the program was connected through the VHL-LISN (VHL-Line Impedance Stabilization Network) to supply the AC mains since it is generally known that the measurement uncertainty is influenced by the termination condition of the cable that goes out of EUT as pointed out in the CISPR16-4-1. As the result of PT-programs, the interval of dispersion in the group formed with the collected data from the participated test sites was 11.6dB at the maximum. Therefore, we concluded the termination of mains cable should be specified with certain common mode impedance such as the VHL-LISN. Consequently, it became easy to find the outlier data of laboratory participated in the PT program.

articleTitle: Ground Discharge Effect to the Sensitive Component in the Charged Board Event Type of Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Functional specifications have usually higher priority than electrostatic discharge (ESD) tolerances and many components are very sensitive to ESD and especially to fast transient pulses during product assembly and manufacturing. Because of the fast rise time of the transient pulse it is quite challenging to evaluate the effect with the standard test methods. The effect of the transient depends also on the surrounding environment and the grounding path. This paper presents a test method for the charged board event (CBE) and shows the effect on a component when the board is discharged from the ground plane. The CBE is studied with 3-D electromagnetic simulations and measurements on a test board. The results indicate that tests can be performed and it is safe to discharge the printed wiring board from the ground plane.

articleTitle: Audio Quality Assessment of Digital Sound Broadcasts in the Presence of Electromagnetic Interferences
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of using automated audio quality assessment methods to measure the effects of electromagnetic interferences on digital sound broadcasts respectively the sound quality degradation. There will be a short introduction to the used algorithm and the basic working principle. With a special setup the determination of the needed interference attenuation for an interference-free broadcast is possible. The introduced concept is helpful in addition to the interference measurement with detectors to ensure vehicular broadcast reception without interferences due to EMC related problems. As an example for the application of this concept is Digital Audio Broadcast (DAB) investigated. The concept is not based on the usually used parameters like: detector readings, radio frequency signal to noise ratios or bit error ratios but on the human perception of sounds. The application of this principle is not limited to a special modulation type.

articleTitle: QUASAR Scenarios for White Space Assessments and Exploitation
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents a unifying scenario classification model and a selection of scenarios, developed within the EU FP7 QUASAR project to study secondary spectrum usage. The classification model categorizes scenarios from technical, regulatory, and economic perspective. It enables the derivation of the most promising scenarios of secondary spectrum access: Cellular and WiFi-like usage of TV white spaces, wireless backhauling using secondary spectrum access, license exempt use of the radar bands, use of the aeronautical bands for mobile broadband and cognitive machine-to-machine communication. These scenarios are presented in more detail along with motivations of why they are interesting to study further. The scenarios will provide the basis for the future work within the QUASAR project, which has the overall objective to assess the amount of useful spectrum opportunities for secondary spectrum access.

articleTitle: Increase the Immunity of an MCU Control Motor System by Detection Method
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper introduces a detection technique to increase the immunity of an MCU control motor system in the complicated EMI environment. The possible interference sources are explained and a test bench for MCU susceptibility measurement is completed. Furthermore a simple detector is introduced to detect the interference on sensitive part of MCU. Finally, the objective of this paper is to divide the MCU work environment into safe mode and unsafe mode by the detection result, and protect the MCU when it work in unsafe mode using defensive software method.

articleTitle: FlexμStrip: A New Measuring Probe for the Characterisation of Large Machines In Situ
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: On the legal aspect, the new European Directive on ElectroMagnetic Compatibility 2004/108/EC concerns also large machines. On a technical point of view, the special situation to characterise the EMC behaviour of large machines imply that current procedures are complex and very expensive, and in some cases even not possible. Adapted measuring methodologies and procedures are needed. In this paper, a new measuring probe is proposed, allowing the characterisation of large machines in situ.

articleTitle: Estimation of Rise Time and Frequency Spectra of Discharge Current Waveforms for Air Discharges of an ESD-Gun with Low Charge Voltages
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The discharge current waveform for air discharges of an ESD-gun with low charge voltages onto a wideband current detector was measured for a bandwidth of 12 GHz. To grasp real rise time of the observed current waveform, input current waveform was estimated from the frequency response of the second order low pass filter of the oscilloscope, which showed that a minimum value of the estimated rise time is 17 ps. Frequency spectra of the estimated current waveforms are also compared with those of measured ones. As a result, for air discharges at several hundred volts, frequency spectra of estimated waveforms have the higher frequency components than measured ones above 2 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Effective Impedance of Micro-Wires Based on Carbon Nanotube Technology
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The skin-effect modeling of isolated micro-wires with rectangular cross-section, consisting of bundles of single wall (SW) or multi-wall (MW) carbon nanotubes (CNTs) is developed. The bundles are treated as homogeneous materials with ac effective conductivity, which is evaluated using the Drude's complex expression. A new formulation is proposed for MWCNT bundles. The frequency-domain distribution of the bundle current density is used to obtain the expressions of the skin depth and of the effective inner impedance. Applications to SWCNT and MWCNT-based micro-wires having different configurations are carried out. The obtained results show the saturation behaviour of the effective inner resistance and inductance above a critical frequency, which depends on the momentum relaxation time of the CNTs.

articleTitle: Estimating an EM Source Location using Freehand Scanning Method for EMF Distributions
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this study, a new scanning method for measuring field distributions is proposed. In this method, measurement positions are automatically decided by a magnetic tracker and recorded to PC. This method obtains field distributions in real-time, and can display field distribution map successively by interpolating. In addition, it has confirmed that an estimating EM source location is possible using the obtained data from this method.

articleTitle: Antenna to Antenna Coupling on an Aircraft using a 1/10th Scale Model with Results Compared to the FEKO Electromagnetic Analysis Program
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Knowing the level of radiation from an antenna and antenna to antenna coupling on an aircraft the potential for cross modulation, in band interference, PIM etc can be determined. Based on this information steps to mitigate these potential EMI problems can be taken, such as provision for filters, % wave traps, RF switches, absorber, or re-location of antennas. Using a 1/10th scale model , computer analysis program or a partial full scale model for this evaluation means that this type of analysis can be performed even before delivery of the aircraft.

articleTitle: Impact of Aging on the Immunity of a Mixed Signal Circuit
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents an original study aiming at evaluating the drift of susceptibility level of a mixed signal circuit during its lifetime. The paper first addresses the issues linked to the experimental set-up and the recommendations required to extract susceptibility level variations. Then the paper presents the evolution of susceptibility after a standard accelerated aging of various digital and analog blocks. While digital blocks remain insensitive to aging, an analog block such as a voltage-controlled oscillator exhibits a significant reduction of its immunity level.

articleTitle: Influence of Aging and Environment Conditions on EMC Performances of Electronic Equipment: Influence of passive Vs active components
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper tries to make in evidence what could be the impact of thermal, aging and tolerances on components characteristics and what could be the consequences on the EMC performances of an automotive equipment. Through particular test cases for emission and immunity analysis, the contributions of passive components are evaluated and compared to preliminary results available on Integrated Circuits (ICs) behavior.

articleTitle: Non-Stationary EMF Standard
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper discusses accuracy of non-stationary EMF measurements. The accuracy is mainly limited by applied methods of meters calibration. New method of calibration is presented. The method allows a limitation of the calibration inaccuracy to level of ±1dB.

articleTitle: A Cross-Layer Approach for Predicting the Effects of Noise on IEEE 802.11g Video Streaming Performance
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Despite the huge development and usage of devices compliant with IEEE 802.11g, their performance is still hard to predict and to guarantee. A lot of work has focused on performance evaluation based on simulations, but it is not sufficient, due to the great number of variables involved. Others have focused on linking the application performance with the channel conditions, however taking into consideration only one end of communication. This paper presents a test bed and a measurement methodology to experimentally analyze the effects of physical layer interference, such as AWG noise, on a scenario that entails an actual, yet simple, IEEE 802.11g network supporting video streaming applications. In addition, the paper presents an initial set of experimental results that help in developing a simple model for correlating physical layer measures to video streaming performance. To this aim, the tests are conducted through a cross-layer approach that allows to compare metrics at different stack layers and predict some network behaviors. The novelty of the model is the fact it considers the noise conditions at both client and server and uses them in a cross-layer approach to predict the video streaming time.

articleTitle: Synchronous versus Asynchronous Circuits Reliability under Radiated Electromagnetic Disturbance
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Nowadays, the major part of electronic devices make use of synchronous circuits controlled by a global clock signal. However, the noise sensitivity as well as the electromagnetic emission of this type of circuit is very high. In this context, asynchronous circuits represent a very interesting solution, since they are naturally more robust than the synchronous counterparts. The proposed work aims at comparing the robustness of synchronous and asynchronous circuits generated according to the Desynchronization Approach presented in [1] when they are exposed to radiated electromagnetic disturbance. Electromagnetic emission levels have also been measured and compared between these two design paradigms. With this purpose, we used as test vehicle a 5-stage pipeline microprocessor, which was implemented in two versions (sync and async) and mapped into a FPGA. The set of experiments was performed according to the IEC 62.132-2 Normative [2].

articleTitle: Practical Application of Satellite Low - Frequency Wave Experiment Results
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The complex analysis of satellite measurement data of low-frequency electromagnetic emission intensity in a frequency range (100 Hz-20 kHz), flow energy electrons, density and temperatures of the ionosphere plasma has shown reaction of ionosphere plasmas on processes of geomagnetic disturbances, preparations of active seismic and slow geodynamic processes. Change of ionosphere plasma parameters, especially, of low- frequency noise intensity, over regions of radioactive pollution is established. The scheme of global satellite monitoring for remote sounding of ecological situation (conditions) for the purpose of revealing of disturbances of natural and technogenic character is offered.

articleTitle: Procedure for Malfunction Detection of Circuits and Systems during Susceptibility Tests
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Monitoring the power supply harmonics of equipment during susceptibility tests provides a powerful tool to detect induced malfunctions especially if statistical techniques are adopted. Immunity problems are identified at their onsets by comparing test results to the susceptibility threshold defined on the basis of an assumed probability of false alarm.

articleTitle: Towards the Generation of Industrial Bundles through a Random Process Under Realistic Constraints
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: To get closer to the reality of aeronautics wire harnesses, we propose to represent a bundle as a non-uniform transmission line by discretizing it into several sections. For each section, positions of conductors are randomized. However this procedure is applied with some geometrical constraints thus resulting in a much more realistic bundle profile. Currents and voltages may be determined on each conductor. Then, we use statistical tools to analyze our results. In order to save computation time, we also propose simplified models for simulation studies of the common mode current.

articleTitle: Statistical Measurements of Fast Changing Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The present works aims at describing important statistical indexes such as the field uniformity, the field inhomogeneity and the statistics near the cavity walls for a special case of fast changing random electromagnetic fields. We generate this kind of electromagnetic environment by means of a vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber. The use of several, fast, in-house, 3-axis field sensors allows for extensive, “real-time” measurements inside such a chamber.

articleTitle: Introducing Mobile Services in the 790-862 MHz Band How Many TV Households Might Suffer from Interference?
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper reports on national investigation of the potential interference to broadcasting channels below 790 MHz when introducing mobile services (e.g. IMT) in the band 790-862 MHz. This investigation is a follow-up of some CEPT studies about regulatory radiation limits which mitigate the impact of adjacent-channel interference from fixed/mobile communication network base stations (BSs) in the 790-862 MHz Digital Dividend spectrum to digital terrestrial television (DTT) services below 790 MHz. Two set of studies have been realized in France to refine these studies taking into account some additional assumptions such a real implementation of IMT base stations, real DTT planning configuration and digital terrain model. An estimation of the number of households which might suffer from interference is also estimated in addition to the percentage of locations. The number of interfered people is in the range of 0.6% (using practical studies) to 2% (using theoretical studies).

articleTitle: Preliminary Studies of the Impact of Dose Radiation on the Electromagnetic Susceptibility of Comparators
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper deals with the susceptibility to high frequency signals in the 600 MHz - 1 GHz frequency range of electronic voltage comparators. The integrated circuits come into two batches: non-irradiated and irradiated by ionizing dose with a cobalt 60 source. Both initial and irradiated devices are then subject to a high frequency perturbation in the near-field zone. Key parameters are then observed. All results are analyzed versus frequency and power of the high frequency aggression. The impact of device bias on the susceptibility threshold is also taken into account.

articleTitle: Spectrum Market or Spectrum Commons?
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper refers to debate about the use and management of radio waves, called shortly the “spectrum”. The paper offers a short review of various viewpoints on privately owned spectrum and collectively owned spectrum and on related spectrum engineering issues.

articleTitle: RFID System Evaluation Against Radiated Transient Noise
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper a radiofrequency identification system according to standard ISO/IEC 14443 type-B is evaluated in presence of transient noise. This real time communication system working at 13.56 MHz is interfered in a controlled environment by different transient bursts varying their level, frequency and duration. The transient burst interference is applied in an AC main wire close to the system and the effect over the digital communication system is evaluated using two different methods. The first one is observing directly an RFID equipment in presence of transient signals, and the second one is capturing the interference in time domain an evaluating its effect by means of simulation. The RFID system is affected by these transient noises causing different types of errors. It is shown that it is essential to measure and evaluate in time domain the transient phenomena to ensure that the RFID system do not have susceptibility problems.

articleTitle: Study for Measurement Methods of Conducted Emission of Communication Ports
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: As disturbance emitted from information technology equipment (ITE), there are radiated disturbance from apparatus, conductive disturbance at communication ports, measuring method is specified in CISPR Pub. 22. About 8-wire types of impedance stabilizing networks (ISNs) for communication port conductive disturbance measurement, the longitudinal conversion loss (LCL) requirements are changed in the 4th and 5th edition. In this paper, the result examined about the composition of ISN, which satisfies the new requirements of the LCL, is described. And also, the limits of conducted disturbances from of communication ports of ITE are specified in this publication. We investigated the evaluation results of measurement methods using this INS, a 150 ohms resistor and a capacitance voltage probe (CVP) whether each measuring methods are adequate for the evaluation of the conducted disturbance at communication ports from ITE.

articleTitle: The Seasonal Abnormal Propagation of VHF/UHF Radio Waves in the West African Sub-Region
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Quite often, due to changes in the atmosphere at a particular time of the year, abnormal propagation of radio waves may occur resulting in harmful interference in radio communications. Commonly referred to as ducting, this phenomenon has serious effect on radio frequency planning methodologies with regard to frequency re-use applications.

articleTitle: The Separation of Superimposed Magnetic Fields using Independent Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, the application of independent component analysis (ICA) on low frequency magnetic fields will be examined. With this method, superimposed magnetic fields can be separated from one another under specific circumstances. Consequently, the magnetic field strength or flux density can be determined separately for various sources. It is also possible with the separation of superimposed field sources to hide individual sources, such as sources of interference. In one example, the data from a field measurement of a power converter controlled drive unit is broken down in such a way that the fields of two sources (currents) are shown separately and can be assessed separately in terms of exposure.

articleTitle: Fine Modeling of Transmission Line Pulse (TLP) and Exploitation for Measurement Set-Up Optimization
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper proposes techniques to model Transmission Line Pulse generator (TLP) in order to able accurate extraction of electrical characteristics of Integrated Circuits (ICs) for behavioral modeling. Exploitation of this model allows the optimization of the test set-up.

articleTitle: Classification and Quantification of Lightning-Current Induced Voltages within Aircraft Structures
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Electromagnetic relations between lightning-currents and induced voltages are reviewed within the context of indirect lightning effects on aircraft structures. Induced voltages are classified according to resistive, inductive, capacitive, and radiated contributions. These separate contributions can be estimated and it turns out that the main lightning current paths of an aircraft structure can be modelled as an RL-network, as long as guidelines of good bonding are observed. Numerical simulations by means of a time domain solver allow calculating lightning-current induced voltages for non-canonical structures and the results confirm the theoretical considerations.

articleTitle: Current and Voltage at Outdoor PLC Ends to Estimate the Radiated Field
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents a simple analytical model to estimate the radiated Held for broadband Power line communication (PLC). One major drawback concern the electromagnetic field radiated by this technology. Indeed, at high frequency, the power lines act as radiating antennas [1]. The case of multiconductor power line is considered with simplified hypothesis: cables are none insulated and the surrounding media is homogenous. The current distribution is derived by using Transmission Line (TL) model. The basic electromagnetic equations are formulated and applied to this line to provide analytical expressions able to compute fields in near and far zone witch is not usually treated. The main topic of this paper is to provide an analytical model applied to bare wires corresponding to classical outdoor transmission lines. For indoor configurations, cables are insulated and the surrounding media is no more homogeneous; this case is treated with a generalized approach and will be proposed in future paper. So the purpose of this paper is to investigate a close-form and accurate computational formulation of the electromagnetic fields radiated at large range of frequencies, as well as to predict the electromagnetic transient effects. In our approach, we avoid to discretize the line and compute the current for each dipole. We consider only near and far end currents and voltages to express analytically the vector potential and to deduce radiated electromagnetic field. Simulation results based on antenna theory [2] are compared to our close-form EM field and shows very good agreement. The result can be generalized to a network of PLC channels, corresponding to real and practical applications. The model is developed using the Frequency Domain (FD) wish is useful to compute with less consuming time realistic scenarios of radiated field in far and near zones.

articleTitle: An Analog Switching (Non PWM) High Power Inverter for EMI Suppression in On-Line Electric Vehicle (OLEV)
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper we introduce the on-line electric vehicle (OLEV) system. We also introduce the non-contact power transfer concept of OLEV and EMI issues that could occur to the power rail of the system. To suppress EMI at the power rail of OLEV system, we propose analog switching concept and analog switching full-bridge inverter, instead of conventional PWM switching inverter. The proposed method is verified by simulation, and it shows that analog switching inverter has better effect on suppressing EMI than conventional switching inverters.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of MIMO UWB Antenna System
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents three matrix models of the antenna structure consisting of two double-element planar antennas for ultra-wideband (UWB) application in MIMO [2x2] indoor communication systems. The thesis presents standard MIMO signal transmission matrix without taking into consideration the coupling between antennas. The electromagnetic model based on the conventional scattering matrix of the MIMO UWB antenna system and a new approach to a full electromagnetic analysis of a MIMO spatial antenna array have been proposed. There have also been presented the results of the computer simulations of different matrices describing the antenna system and the transmission propagation pulses in the whole system.

articleTitle: Simplified Modeling of Complex Cable Bundles with Inhomogeneous Cable Paths
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this contribution, the procedure “Equivalent Cable Bundle Method” is used for the simplification of large cable bundles, and it is extended to the application on inhomogeneous cable paths. Furthermore, the effect of a modified consideration of the current distribution within the cables bundle is evaluated. It is shown that that the analyzed approach can be used to generate simplified cable bundles for aribtrary routing geometries. The susceptibility of the simplified cable bundles and the original ones is equivalent.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of EMI Caused by Charged Human Walking Near by Electronic System
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper reports the experimental analysis of charge induction phenomena on floating metals in the electronic system caused by walking charged human and EMI (electromagnetic interference) on digital circuits because of a small gap discharge.

articleTitle: Determination of the Complex Permittivity of Dispersive Materials Without Assuming a Dielectric Relaxation Model
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents a procedure to extract the complex relative permittivity of a dispersive material without assuming a dielectric relaxation model. To assess and validate the procedure, published experimental data for methanol were considered. The frequency behaviour of the extracted complex relative permittivity is in good agreement with that of three classic dielectric relaxation models (Havriliak-Negami, Cole-Cole and Debye models). The advantage of this approach is noticeable when applied to new developed materials or materials whose frequency dependence is not known a priori. A proper dielectric relaxation model can be chosen and easily built over the whole frequency range of measurement through a quick interpolation of the complex relative permittivity values found.

articleTitle: The Generation of UWB Pulses with High Repetition Rates for Immunity Tests
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this contribution a generator for ultra wideband pulses with high repetition rates for immunity tests and investigations with protection elements is presented. This paper contains the special generator principle with measurement and simulation results and first investigations with protection elements, which are exposed to the generated UWB pulse signals.

articleTitle: Emissions from Automation Equipment Regarding Human Exposure: Approaches for an Assessment According to the Generic Standard IEC 62311
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In many countries and regions there are specified requirements regarding electromagnetic emissions from electrical equipment. Limitation of such emissions which is one task within the area of EMC activities is mostly due to the need to protect radio services from being interfered. Applicable limits depend on the type of the equipment being considered and of the class of the location where equipment is intended to be operated. However, such emissions are also being increasingly assessed from a human exposure point of view within the framework of EMF regulations. Both aspects deal with entirely disparate objective targets. As a consequence, different limits, diverse measurement procedures and divergent assessment methods are to be applied. In practice, this could mean that basically two kinds of measurements have to be carried out. This paper introduces a possible approach of how results obtained by means of EMC measurements can also be used for the purpose of EMF assessments. It divides the whole frequency range from 0 Hz to 300 GHz into several frequency bands with various assessment approaches done in those frequency bands.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Approach used to Analyze the EMC Performance of a ZVS Converter
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, a hierarchical approach is proposed for EMI level prediction. The difficulties of EMI modeling of the AC-AC converters due to the special characteristics of the applications are first pointed out. Present methods are reviewed next. Then, the proposed method is introduced. The steps of applying this approach are demonstrated for a ZVS converter. Because this approach is a straight forward method, it gives a possibility to do optimization and sensitivity analysis for EMC issue of power electronic application.

articleTitle: Lightning Test on an Electronic Lamp Driver
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Two electronic drivers for gas-discharge lamps have been tested for the immunity of lightning induced common mode currents. A series of tests with increasing threat level have been applied, given equipment available in the TU/e high-voltage laboratory. One type of unit turned out to be damaged by CM currents of the order of 100 A. This unit proved also quite sensitive to lightning in practice. The other unit remains functional with 2.5 kA.

articleTitle: The Effects of the EMC-Wooden Table on Single-Wire Wave (Sommerfeld Wave)
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper the effects of the wooden table, which is used in EMC (Electromagnetic Compatibility) measurements, on the single-wire wave propagation on uncoated metal wire (Sommerfeld wave) in frequency range from 100 to 1000 MHz are investigated. The measured results were performed for the same arrangement with and without the wooden table (air) and for different distances between the wooden table and the single-wire transmission line.

articleTitle: Fine Analysis of the Behavior of a Reverberation Chamber in the Frequency Domain with a Model Based Upon Image Theory
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this article, we propose a model based upon image theory (IT). This very straightforward model designed initially as a time domain model carry the physics of a reverberation chamber (RC) and is able to simulate its behavior in the frequency domain. Simulation results obtained with this model are compared with measurements in the reverberation chamber of our laboratory and an electric field imbalance observed in our reverberation chamber is reproduced with our model.

articleTitle: Intentional Electromagnetic Interferences and EMC Problems: THz Waves-EMC Strategy for the Future
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The future of utilization of the new terahertz frequency bands needs the concept of autonomous Terahertz stationary/mobile communication network-centric systems with Cognitive Radio Software nodes to conduct ultra wide digital transmission and to apply in High Power Electromagnetics (HPEM) environment including High Altitude Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) and Intentional Electromagnetic Interferences (IEMI). In military and security terms it could be the electromagnetic warfare and electromagnetic terrorism environment, including the use of HEMP, especially HPM (High Power Microwave) and DEW (Directed Energy Weapons). High Power Electromagnetic threats coexist with Cyberwar and Cybercrime.

articleTitle: A Simulation Flow for Time Domain Magnetic Radiations of ICs
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: If for many years ElectroMagnetic (EM) radiations of Integrated Circuits (IC) constitute a main problem from an ElectroMagnetic Compatibility (EMC) point-of-view, it is now also a critical problem for secure IC designers. Indeed, EM radiations of an IC, and more precisely the magnetic component, can be exploited to retrieve sensible data such as, the secret key of cryptographic algorithms. Within this context, this paper aims at introducing a magnetic field simulation flow allowing predicting, with high spatial and time resolutions, the magnetic radiations of IC cores. Such a flow being mandatory to predict the robustness of secure ICs before fabrication against EM attacks.

articleTitle: Equivalent Source Correspending to Radiated Field of EMC Filter Components
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: EMC Filters are increasingly integrated into power applications. To improve their performances it is important to model the electromagnetic interference between components to optimize their positions in the filter. In this paper, a method is proposed to construct the equivalent models of the component radiated field. The method proposed is based on the multipolar expansion, which provides us reduced models for the field radiated by generic structures. These models of the sources will be used to compute the mutual inductance between the components according to their geometrical placement.

articleTitle: Methodology for Establishing Intensity Level Maps of Electromagnetic Fields in Hospitals
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: An important issue to consider when planning building a hospital is the electromagnetic fields which will be present. High signal peaks could generate unwanted electromagnetic interferences in electro-medical equipment, which may result in a wrong diagnosis or treatment for the patient, and also an over-exposition for workers and physicians. In this work, a new methodology for the generation of intensity level maps of electromagnetic fields taken in each unit of a hospital is proposed. A set of samples situated on a grid of a certain dimension is collected, and processed subsequently. Several level curves have been obtained, showing that this methodology could help in the design of new health centres.

articleTitle: Application of Nanostructured Materials Ensuring the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Power Electronic
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The processes of screening of electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields in the frequency range: units, tens of kilohertz to few, tens of gigahertz are considered. The requirements to the nanostructure composite materials for electromagnetic screening are described. Methods for the screens implementation on the basis of reflecting or absorbing broadband nanocomposite structures are identified.

articleTitle: PCB Level Wireless Wide Area Networking Approach for Netbook Applications
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The solutions proposed in this paper are useful in the detection of Wireless Wide Area Networking (WWAN) interference in netbook applications, as they facilitated a reduction in EMI level of 5-9 dB in WWAN frequency bands. In addition, analysis of all noise sources from LED driver IC, T-con, source IC, and scan driver pulses may be helpful in solving the WWAN EMI interference problem of TFT-LCD modules within various netbook systems. The proposed solution was tested on the 10.1” netbook module, which is the main stream component of netbook. The resolution is 1024 x 600 pixels, the gate turn-on voltage is 20.1 V, and the turn-off voltage is -13 V.

articleTitle: Customisable Mains Filter for Educational Purposes
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper presents a conception of a low cost educational platform for designing and evaluating the suppression characteristic of custom-made mains filters (power line filters). It is universal, compact and robust construction dedicated for educational purposes. The main goal of the presented platform is to provide students with a basic understanding of EMC issues in the field of the mains filter design and evaluation methods thereof.

articleTitle: Coefficient of Variation in Time and Spatial EMF Measurements Near Transmitting Stations
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The coefficient of variation (CoV) has been examined for measurements of electromagnetic fields (EMF) near high and medium power transmitting/base stations in Poland. The time and spatial variation of signals at points of investigation (POI) has been measured for different locations and for different radiocommunication systems. It has been found that the time variation of signals in the far field region has low value (CoV < 11%). The spatial variation, considered as the change within the cube of size of 0,6m x 0,8m x 0,8m, is higher (CoV < 33%) but is still low. It means that the probability that the human exposure assessment will be incorrect because of improper choice of the measurement time or location of probe in each POI is relatively low.

articleTitle: Static Source-Mode Tuning using a Constellation of LPDA Antennas in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: An innovative source-mode tuning of electromagnetic fields in a reverberation chamber (RC) is presented. This is based on an antenna network placed in the RC. The fixed antennas are commuted sequentially rather than using a moving mechanical stirrer like a rotary paddle wheel. The objective is to get rid of any moving part and to decrease the testing time. A review of stirrer types is made. The efficiency of the new stirrer is assessed as a function of the field uniformity requirements of the IEC 61000-4-21 which states the 3 dB limit above 400 MHz. In our case we will work within the frequency band of mobile phone and GPS systems (800-2500 MHz). The three components of the E- field, the forward and reverse output powers and the binary code associated with the emitting antennas have been acquired for each of the tuner positions, at eight locations delimiting the testing volume, and at the number of frequencies as required in the standard. The first results show a promising method for tuning in an RC as the field uniformity complies with the standard deviation requirement of the IEC 61000-4-21.his electronic document is a “live” template.
