articleTitle: Wideband Measurement of Radiated Electromagnetic Field Intensity Caused by Low Voltage ESD
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The micro-gap discharge as the low voltage ESD shows very fast transition duration of about 32 ps or less. Besides, breakdown electric field strength between the gap was examined to corroborate the very fast transition durations of about 32ps. As a consequence of the experiment, the breakdown field strength in the gap was very high of about 80 MV/m in low voltage discharging of below 350. Also, a relationship between the breakdown field strength in the gap and radiated electromagnetic field intensity was examined in experimental study. The relative radiated electromagnetic field intensity was proportion to the breakdown field strength at the gap in the resonance experimental system using the discharge electrode with dipole configuration. In this time, we present an improved experimental system to measure the radiated electromagnetic filed intensity in more wideband region using spherical electrodes and a horn antenna.

articleTitle: Broadband Matching Windows for Waveguide SAR Calibration Systems to Span 1.7 GHz to 5.85 GHz
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Mobile phones and other wireless products used in close proximity to the body must be tested to ensure that the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of radio frequency energy in the user remains below internationally specified safety limits. Electric field probes used for such measurements must be calibrated in tissue simulating liquid, and the matched waveguide systems used for this purpose are narrow-band. This paper presents new matching window designs, which allow calibration to be performed over the majority of the waveguide band. Three waveguide systems were developed to cover the frequency range 1.7 GHz to 5.85 GHz. The design of the matching window section gives maxima in the input return loss at two separate frequencies. In this way a return loss of greater than 8 dB is achieved across most of the operating band of the waveguide using two matching windows. The calibration uncertainties for the systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Efficient EMI-Filters for High-Current Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Power converters generate electromagnetic interferences (EMI) in form of both conducted and radiated disturbances. These electromagnetic emissions are best reduced at their source and by additional shielding and filtering. Passive filtering of conducted emissions is well understood. However, the design of volume- and weight optimized solutions with significant current ratings and appropriate filter-attenuation needs to be addressed and is not available as off-the-shelf solution. This paper presents compact high-current filter solutions for mobile applications and describes their impact concerning the reduction of EMI. In particular, passive and active filters against common-mode interferences are discussed for 28VDC interfaces and 10-30 kW power applications.

articleTitle: Research on Conductive Interference Control for Station Track Circuit in Datong-Qinhuangdao Heavy-Haul Railway
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: To alleviate conductive interference of unbalanced traction current on ZPW-2000A track circuit under the condition of 20 000 tons heavy haul in station of Datong-Qinhuangdao electric railway, a solution based on impedance-match apparatus was designed, featuring air-gap transformer with double function LC filter circuit. It appears below 0.01Ω at resonating power frequency 50Hz and yet more than 17Ω at signal frequencies. The characteristics intrinsically not only assure anti-interference performance, but also meet the requirement of signal transmission. Both system experiments and field application demonstrated the solution was feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Caused by Wireless Body Area Network to Medical Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this study, the influence of communication signals on an electrode for electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring was examined. A signal, that is assumed to be from a wireless body area network (WBAN), is transmitted to the electrode on a phantom. The difference in receiving power under various measurement conditions is examined, such as distance, frequency, and the number of electrodes. The distance between the electrode and WBAN antenna was set at 3 cm, 5 cm, or 10 cm. The operating frequencies were set at 403.5 MHz, 444.5 MHz, 953 MHz, and 2450 MHz at the WBAN antenna. One or two electrodes were under the examination. Result shows that only for 403.5 MHz, the distance characteristic is different from those at other frequencies, in the case of one electrode. The distance characteristics are different for each frequency considered, in the case of two electrodes. In particular, the signals induced on the electrode in the case of 953 MHz were considerably weaker than those at other frequencies.

articleTitle: Load Cells Utilization in MEG Environment: A Feasibility Study by Electromagnetic Characterization and Shielding
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The low intensity of the magnetic field generated by the brain (several tens of femto Tesla) makes the use of rehabilitation robotic systems (with load cells as components) extremely challenging in MEG environment. The interference generated by load cells has indeed an intensity able to “hide” cerebral signals. In the present study we analyze the electromagnetic interference generated by a 6-axis force/torque sensor (load cell) and its cables (frequency range 50 Hz - 3 GHz). Firstly the radiated emission by a load cell is characterized. Then, an appropriate aluminium shielding is designed assuming the value of 0.50 pT as the maximum acceptable magnetic field not shadowing cerebral signals. A positive test in MEG environment of the shielded load cell, suggests the possibility to replace the hydraulic and pneumatic transducers, currently employed to avoid electromagnetic interference, with electronic ones.

articleTitle: ESD Arc Analysis and System-Level Simulation
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This work demonstrates a simple experiment setup to measure ESD arc currents and presents how the current waveforms change by the distance between the target and the tip of ESD generator. And it also gives an EM-field simulation model of a commercial ESD generator (Dito from EM-Test) for characterizing for arc waveform. In order to achieve the EM- field simulation model, the critical factors shall be discussed to correlate to measurement.

articleTitle: Deterministic Coefficient of Electronic System Strenght on Electromagnetic Disturbances
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In paper problem of strength (reliability) determining of electronic elements and circuit on normalized disturbing signal has been formulated in theoretical and practical aspects. The method of strength (reliability) coefficient estimation for chosen system and its components has been proposed. The theoretical considerations were experimentally verified by analysis of the test system (dimmer of halogen lamps) for selected 1.2/50 µs surge levels.

articleTitle: Lightning Current Tests to Evaluate Vulnerability of Electronics in Composite Structures
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Protecting highly sensitive electronics housed inside composite structures against lightning is a real challenge. The direct strike represents the worst-case scenario for composite structures. The electromagnetic field generated by an indirect lightning strike in the vicinity of highly sensitive equipment can cause interference or even damage electronic components. The Military Standard MIL STD - 464A gives some indications about the characteristics of a lightning strike (negative in polarity). A first discharge of 50 to 200kA, called A Pulse followed by two subsequent B & C Pulses. The B Pulse has a current of 2 kA while Pulse C has between 200 and 800 A. A test setup capable to replicate these characteristics is used to perform various tests on structures that replicate radars.

articleTitle: Active Shield to Minimize Magnetic Flux Density for On-Line Electric Vehicle (OLEV) Application
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the on-line electric vehicle (OLEV) system and its non-contact power transfer mechanism, and propose active magnetic shielding method for the reduction of magnetic flux from the power line and pickup module of the vehicle. We analyzed the effect of active shields placed in the vehicle and underneath the surface of the road. By selecting active shield underground and by optimizing position and current, the leakage magnetic flux has been significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the Reverberation Chamber Method for the Measurement of Material Absorbing Cross Section
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Reverberation chamber (RC) test facility allows to determine the absorbing cross section (ACS) of lossy materials under a random field excitation. Measurements are based on the quality factor variation produced by the sample under test presence with respect to the empty chamber condition. Simulations are based on the representation of the RC electromagnetic field by means of a random plane wave superposition. A finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) code is used to compute the material absorbed power and to recover a numerical ACS. The method sensibility is stressed by application to small size samples. Comparison between numerical and experimental data reveals a satisfactory agreement. The simulation technique can be applied to study the absorbing properties of absorbers with arbitrary geometry during the early design stage.

articleTitle: Features of Power-Line Impedance Effects on EMI Filter Performance
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents the effect estimation of power-line impedance on the filter performance at a frequency range from 9 kHz to 30 MHz. In this paper proposed the requirements for microprocessor control to determine the power-line impedance in real-state to following changes for EMI filters. On the basis of analysis of known methods of power-line impedance determination developed algorithm for CPU of EMI filter operation.

articleTitle: Outage Statistics Based Analysis of Sectored Mobile System as a Spectrum Efficient Congestion Control Technique
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Spectral occupancy and congestion control in cellular communication system have been the subject of increasing attention in present environment. Cellular structure induces the co channel interference. Sectoring is an effective way for reducing co channel interference. In the paper co channel interference induced outage statistics in sectored cell structure are computed and then analyzed. Outage statistics like outage probability and outage time varies with variation in SNR threshold, Cluster size and number of sectors. Monte Carlo technique is used for simulation purpose. Results demonstrate that the sectorisation lowers the outage probability by almost 20 % as number of sectors increase from 3 to 6. As the cluster size is reduced from 7 to 4 outage probability almost doubles on reverse link and triples on forward link for omni directional case. The derived information can be further applied for congestion control algorithm designing, efficient spectrum allocation policies and higher order protocol performance evaluation of the mobile network.

articleTitle: Modeling of Automotive Bus Transceivers and ESD Protection Circuits for Immunity Simulations of Extended Networks
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: To establish a stable communication between electronic control units in vehicles special bus systems were developed. CAN and FlexRay are safe data buses with high immunity against electromagnetic disturbances. To ensure the safety, the systems should be qualified with special RF immunity tests, e.g. BCI, within the development process. EMC simulations can help to calculate the effect of electromagnetic disturbances coupled to the bus system cable network. To protect the transceiver on PCB level against ESD, additional overvoltage protection elements are often used. However, the non linear ESD protection circuits and high disturbance levels can change the shape of the bus signal and the transceivers may not be able to detect the bus information. For simulation based EMC investigations using large BCI setups exact models of the wires, the ESD protection elements, the behavior of the transceivers, and the BCI injection clamp are necessary. These models were developed and verified with measurements. The simulation results are in good agreement with measurements.

articleTitle: A Monte-Carlo Simulation of Mode-Stirred Chambers with Standing Waves
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A plane wave representation for the fields inside an ideal mode-stirred chamber is known from [1]. The superposition of plane waves satisfies both the Maxwell equations and the statistic distribution and spatial correlation of the field quantities. As the mode-stirred chamber is a cavity resonator, whose eigenmodes can be described by standing waves, a standing wave representation is also possible. Similarly from the plane wave approach a standing wave representation is deducable, since two plane wave with the same amplitude traveling in antiparallel directions form a standing wave. In the following paper it is shown that the plane wave and standing wave approach are analytically completely equivalent and numerically very similar.

articleTitle: A Time Domain Noise Reduction Filter in Analog Signal Acquisition Interface for Temperature Sensors
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Isolated signal acquisition systems are often used in the field of the industrial factory automation. In order to improve the quality of analog signals from temperature sensors, a noise reduction filter is essential at the signal acquisition interface. In this paper, a time domain noise reduction filter, composed of analog integration circuit, is proposed for the signal acquisition interface in which transformer isolation method is used. It is shown that the proposed filter satisfies the required condition of settling time: 100 µs and noise rejection ratio of 30 dB in the frequency range of over 100 kHz. Also, from the comparison results of conventional Butterworth filter and proposed time domain filter, the proposed filter achieves better performance of noise reduction ratio in the frequency range of below 1000 kHz. Also, the proposed filter has good rejection ratio to the cyclic noise, which arises from DC-DC converters, if the fundamental frequency of the noise is aligned to multiple integer of inverse of acquisition time of the filter.

articleTitle: Safety Aspects of a System for Heart Stimulation Induced by a Magnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A system for heart stimulation induced by a magnetic pulse has been designed. It is characterized by high intensity current pulses, and therefore safety may arise for operators and medical devices during its use. In particular, in this contribution safety considerations are analyzed and shielding actions are proposed in order to make cardiac stimulation available in hospital environment.

articleTitle: Impedance Stabilization Networks by using Asymmetrical Transformer: For More Accurate Conducted Disturbances Measurement on Power Line
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes an impedance stabilization network (ISN) that simulates low longitudinal conversion loss (LCL) cables such as AC mains lines. Current ISNs used to measure conducted disturbance from information technology equipment are limited in that they cannot measure the disturbance on low LCL cables precisely. We propose and evaluate a new ISN using an asymmetrical transformer. The experimental results show that the ISN satisfies the requirements discussing for international standardization in CISPR/I/PT-PLT for the majority of the required frequency range. Moreover, conducted disturbance voltages and currents emitted from a PLT modem are measured. The results show that the proposed ISN can be used to measure disturbance voltage.

articleTitle: Analytic Iterative Approach to Crosstalk Analysis of Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: An analytic iterative solution in the frequency domain is proposed for crosstalk on multiconductor transmission lines. The proposed method employs the distributed analytical representation of equivalent coupling sources and an iterative technique. The effects of adjacent lines at each iteration are considered as equivalent distributed sources along the lines. These equivalent distributed sources are further implemented analytically, leading to a more efficient updating process. The dependance on the coupling factors and the length of the line was investigated, in order to assess the computational efficiency and the accuracy of the advocated method, as compared to classical solutions in terms of decoupling matrix.

articleTitle: Measurement of Power Frequency Electric and Magnetic Fields Nearby Power Facilities in Several Countries
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Although it is important to actually measure the power frequency electric and magnetic fields (EMF) inside and around power facilities to evaluate them quantitatively, there seems to have been no systematic research of this kind. Under such a circumstance, the authors have planned and been carrying out international cooperative research among various countries on power frequency electric and magnetic fields measurements. This paper describes the results of the EMF measurement inside and around power facilities in Colombia, Cuba, Indonesia, Japan, Mexico, Thailand, and USA.

articleTitle: The Influence of Power Network Conductive Disturbances on Operation of the Inductive Current Transformers
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In the accurate measurement of currents significant values current transformers are being used. During estimation of the power quality their should also maintain a given accuracy of transformation for transient states and conductive disturbances which occurs during interruptions and dips in the supply voltage of the current transformer primary circuit. Determine of the conductive disturbances level in this circuit on the basis of measurements of secondary current requires information about the accuracy of distorted currents transfer by used current transformer. For this purpose transfer characteristic on the base of measurements of the conductive disturbances particular harmonics rms values in the currents and voltages on primary and secondary sides of the tested CT were determine. In this article results of measurements as well as conclusions from analysis of the influence of the power network conductive disturbances on operation of the tested current transformer with toroidal core made from NiFe 78 permalloy are presented.

articleTitle: Accuracy of the Current Transformer with Toroidal Core for Distorted Currents Transformation
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: One of the main factors in determining the metrological characteristics of the current transformers is the accuracy class assigned for sinusoidal signals of frequency 50 Hz. The aim of the project is to develop a methodology of instrument transformers standardization for distorted signals transfer. In order to ensure proper assessment of the current higher harmonic level in the power networks were hall effect sensors can not be used instrument transformers should ensure a fixed accuracy of the distorted currents transformation. Analysis of this transfer accuracy were made on the example of the current transformer with toroidal core made from permalloy NiFe 78. Developed method allows to determine the accuracy of the current transformer in the evaluation of the power quality and estimation of the primary current conducted disturbances level.

articleTitle: Repetition Rate and Pulse Width Influence on Electromagnetic Effects
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Some results obtained during experimental measurements of susceptibility of electronics to HPM and UWB irradiation with repetition rate signals are presented in this paper. Repetition rate dependence is considered for temporary failures as well as for damage levels too. As equipments under test are chosen regular PC setups. Simple electronic circuits are added for some experiments for possibility to achieve more results related to damage levels. Suitable simplified circuit models for HPM and UWB repetition rate effectiveness for achieving of typical effects on electronics is used for simulations. For this purpose model based on electrothermal analogy is used within the software OrCAD 15.7 (PSpice model) environment. Results from measurements are compared with results from simulations. At the end of this presentation recommendation for effective HPM and UWB rep-rate necessary to achieve typical failures of tested equipments is carried out.

articleTitle: Differential to Common Mode Conversion in Balanced Devices and Systems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The problem of differential mode to common mode conversion in balanced devices and systems is illustrated. The mixed mode S parameters are not suitable to characterize this mechanism and what is more important they do not allow an easy interpretation of common mode and differential mode losses. Mixed mode Z parameters provide the right tool to achieve a better insight into problems related to EMC matters. On the other hand S parameters are more suitable to be measured and to characterize cascaded devices. The mode conversion does not only depend on imbalances in the electrical signal transmission paths but also may be caused by amplitude, delay and waveform skews in differential sources; the combination of imbalances of the differential signals and of the transmission paths generates common mode signals. Simulation results are presented and discussed to illustrate the previous conclusions.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Ultra-Wideband Leading Edge Detection Positioning Receivers
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper deals with the evaluation of leading edge detection receivers intended for the time difference of arrival measurements in ultra-wideband positioning systems. The paper addresses receiver sensitivity and co-channel rejection of impulse ultra-wideband interference. Presented analysis is based on the results of leading edge detection receiver measurements. The paper contains a proposal for criteria for the receiver evaluation.

articleTitle: The Maximum Impulsiveness Correction Factor for Middleton's Class a Interference for Different Modulation Schemes
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Simplified algorithms used to determine the performance of digital radio communication systems is desirable. Such simplified algorithms can for example be used in telecommunication performance analysis tools and in frequency measurements to study the impact from disturbances and interference from other users in the dynamic spectrum access (DSA) applications. Today, existing methods are relatively complicated and time-consuming when performance is calculated for interference environments with impulse-rich character. A correction factor (impulsiveness correction factor, ICF) has previously been proposed which opens up for simplified approximations in performance calculations. Using the correction factor in the so-called Gaussian approximation of interference signal provides that simple performance formulas can be used. In this work, the correction factor has been derived for a wider group of interference signals and radio systems which means that its usefulness in practical solutions has increased significantly.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Shielding Effectiveness Degradation
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The shielding effectiveness of an enclosure degrades due to aging effects and also because mechanical joints, fixtures and jumpers become looser and looser. It has been recognized [1] that shielding maintenance is an important issue in the automotive and aeronautical field because it may affect the safety condition of passengers. Moreover it is important to maintain shielding integrity in those rooms where confidential data are processed.

articleTitle: Whole-Body Averaged SAR Measurement for Postured Japanese Human Models using Cylindrical-External Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The purpose of this study is to establish a whole-body averaged specific absorption rate (WB-SAR) experimental estimation method using the total power absorbed by humans; a cylindrical-external field scanning technique is used to measure the radiated RF (radio-frequency) power. This technique is adopted with the goal of simplifying the exposure dosimetry of humans of different postures and/or sizes. We have carried out experimental estimations using constructed SAR measurement system for standing and sitting human models.

articleTitle: Fundamental Properties of Non-Cuboid Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Electromagnetic reverberation chambers were proposed in 1968 by Mendez [8] and have been discussed as possible ways for radiated immunity and emission tests since then. Continuous use lead to demand for standardization, which was covered by the publication of the IEC standard 61000-21-4 [2] in 2001. Since electromagnetic reverberation chambers were developed to replace semi-anechoic chambers or open area test facilities for testing of large scale DUTs, most of the initial research was devoted to large cuboid chambers. Yet, if a smaller chamber is needed (for lack of lab space, for example) or if the use of (expensive) amplifiers is to be avoided, the IEC standard will provide only suboptimal information for this. Furthermore, the possibility to use other geometrical bodies was not yet investigated in depth. Some of the cavity resonators that could be used as a basis for reverberation chambers have a better surface to volume ratio and thereby promise to have a higher quality by default. Additionally, is to be expected that the superposition of different resonant modes will result in larger test volume (read: volume in which fields are homogenous and evenly distributed w.r.t direction and polarization), since the directions of the fields inside a non-cuboid volume will be irregular. Therefore, it should be possible to reduce the size of the chambers even more. In this paper we first discuss a relatively small cuboid cavity which we will use as a reference. Then we review chambers based on cylinders with circular and elliptic cross sections, spheres, and finally scalene ellipsoids. For these bodies, eigenmodes and eigenfrequencies are calculated numerically and analytically (if possible). The mode densities and qualities are determined.

articleTitle: Dynamic Spectrum Management for Military Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A rapidly growing demand for services accessed by wireless networks triggers calls to have the efficient tools for spectrum allocation during mission planning and supervision. Two architectures (CJSMPT, DIMSUMNet) for legacy and modernized equipment are described. An opportunistic spectrum access is the most promising method for future cognitive radio networks (CRN) and therefore this paper deals with a general cognitive radio (CR) concept, as well as some standardization works concerning cognitive and dynamic spectrum access.

articleTitle: Stealth Systems on Classic and Electromagnetic Battlefields and Problem of Coexisting Systems Survivability during Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI): Stealth System as Specific Kind of EM Compatible systems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: International EMI divide systems between friendly systems and enemy systems which does not depend on us. But exists a huge technology area stealth or stealthy systems which minimizes risk of IEMI influence on friendly systems.
