articleTitle: Optimised Equivalent Dipole Model of PCB Emissions Based on Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A method for optimising the modeling of electromagnetic emissions from printed circuits with equivalent dipole sources is presented. The optimization procedure is based on a genetic algorithm which is used to determine the number of equivalent dipoles and their parameters by fitting to the measured near fields. Prediction of emissions from the PCB can then be obtained by computing from the equivalent model without reference to the details of the PCB. It is shown that by using a novel mutually competitive evolution between two populations a high degree of optimisation is achieved that provides useful insights into this form of emissions model and the location of specific emission centres.

articleTitle: Far Field Estimations and Simulation Model Creation from Cable Bundle Scans
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The emission level of automotive systems is often governed by the cable harness, it is often the dominant radiating structure and determines the position of resonances. The established field measurement methods according CISPR 25 for evaluation of emissions suffer from the need to use large anechoic chambers. Furthermore measurement data can not be used for simulation model creation in order to compute the overall fields radiated from a car. In this paper a simple method to determine the far-fields and a simulation model of a radiating cable bundle from near-field measurements is proposed. The method measures the electromagnetic fields at several points near to a cable bundle. Measurements are done in time domain in order to get phase information, to reduce measurement time, and to correlate different measurement data sets. From the field measurement data an equivalent current distribution in a cable bundle can be computed. With this information a simulation model of the setup can be generated, far-field estimations can be done.

articleTitle: RF Coupling in CMOS Analog Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents the susceptibility of CMOS analog integrated circuits to electromagnetic interferences (EMIs) The disturbances are superimposed to an adjacent line (aggressor line) and couple via capacitive coupling mechanisms to a sensitive track of an analog circuit (victim line). For this purpose various circuits have been designed and manufactured in a Bipolar- CMOS-DMOS-technology (BCD) for automotive applications. Actuating variables that influence the susceptibility of nets are discussed. Ones sensitive nets are known routing strategies or filtering can be applied to increase the immunity of the endangered analog circuit which results consequently in an immunity increase of the integrated circuit.

articleTitle: Exploiting Planes of Magnetic Symmetry in the Fast Multipole Method
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: For the analysis of typical frequency-domain problems in EMC the method of moments (MoM) [1] is frequently used. The amount of memory required for a simulation is growing with the square of the number of unknowns N and the computation time is even growing with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Because of this the classic MoM is only of limited applicability for the investigation of extended objects. In order to be able to analyze electrically large objects acceleration methods have to be applied which are capable to reduce the memory and time requirement of a MoM simulation. The fast multipole method (FMM) is such an approach [2], having a complexity of O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) for both time and memory in its one level version. The focus of this paper is the exploitation of magnetic symmetry planes in an FMM-based analysis. It turns out that exploiting symmetry improves the performance of the numerical analysis yielding a reduction of computation time and memory requirement by more than 50%.

articleTitle: Modelling and Measurement of Crosstalk between Shielded Cables
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A technique for modeling coaxial cables which may be embedded in a range of time domain full field electromagnetic field prediction codes is described. The coaxial cable model is linked to a TLM field code and applied to the analysis of crosstalk between coaxial cables. Comparison is made with measurements performed at the University of Nottingham.

articleTitle: Redundancy Concept to Increase Transmission Reliability in WLAN Systems: Redundance-Transmission of Navigation Data via WLAN on Ships
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this contribution a wireless data transmission system is introduced for the transmission of navigation data on the bridge of vessels. The propagation behavior of WLAN on the bridge is shortly discussed as well as the influence of possible interferences. Because of the possible effects of interferences to the performance of the wireless link and due to the fact that navigation data is security-relevant different redundancy concepts are presented to ensure a reliable data transmission. The developed redundant data transmission system is introduced and tested at the laboratory and on board of a modern cruise vessel. The improvement compared to non-redundant systems has also been investigated.

articleTitle: On the use of Reverberation Chamber to Simulate the Power Delay Profile of a Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide some further observations on the use of reverberation chambers to imitate real wireless channels. It is shown, that when RMS delay spread is calculated appropriate threshold has to be chosen. Based on the threshold value the required dynamics of measurements performed for realistic wireless channels can be estimated. It is also shown, that the reverberation chamber loading method allows only for representing outdoor channels.

articleTitle: Calculation of Whole-Body Average SARs in Infant Models for Far-Field Exposure over GHz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: With much concern about health effects of children for radio-wave exposure, computational studies on whole-body averaged specific absorption rates (WBA-SARs) in anatomically based child models have actively been conducted. For different electromagnetic polarization, we calculated WBA-SARs up to 15 GHz in the Japanese models of 3-year-old child, and 9-month-old and 0-month-old infants with a resolution of 1 mm/0.25 mm. Then, WBA-SARs obtained herein are compared with those estimated from our formula proposed in our previous study. As a result, we found that horizontal exposure polarization provides larger WBA-SARs in infant models than that for the vertical one. The WBA-SARs have rather flat characteristics in the frequency range from 1 GHz to 3 GHz, which become almost constant over 10 GHz. It was also found that the WBA-SARs estimated from the formula are conservative for different exposure polarization. The finding obtained suggests that the reference level at 0.8 GHz in general public exposure is more appropriate levels to limit WBA-SAR for frequencies above a few gigahertzes.

articleTitle: Validation of the MoM Simulation Model for GTEM Including Pyramid Absorber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Since the publication of IEC 61000-4-20, the gigahertz transverse electromagnetic (GTEM) cell has gained popularity in radiated emission and immunity electromagnetic compatibility tests. Various numerical methods such as finite difference time domain, finite element method and transmission line matrix have been used to model the GTEM cell in the pursuit of getting to know the characteristic of the GTEM cell with varying degrees of verification. In this paper, the method of moments will be used to model the GTEM cell including the pyramid absorber. The simulation model was validated by comparison with measured electromagnetic fields in the cell. The analytical field calculations for higher order modes in the GTEM cell 1750 were compared with the simulation results. Additionally, the influence of the presence of the pyramid absorber was investigated in this contribution. Good agreement between the experimental results and simulations has been obtained.

articleTitle: A Multi-Channel, FFT-Based, Amplitude Probability Distribution Measuring Instrument
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Technical details of a multi-channel, FFT-based, amplitude probability distribution (APD) measuring instrument are described in this paper. We had previously reported that multi-channel APD of electromagnetic disturbance measured in each sub-channel of wireless communication system using OFDM leads to BER degradation of the communication system interfered by the disturbance, however, there has been no instrument that realizes a multi-channel APD measurement over hundreds, possibly thousands frequency channels. The developed multi-channel APD measuring instrument has two operating modes called ‘WLAN mode’ and ‘DTV mode’. The WLAN mode enables to evaluate APD in 64 sub-channels whose frequency spacing is 312.5 kHz. In the DTV mode, measurement of APD in 8192 channels with spacing of 992 Hz is realized. Practical application of the instrument is also shown in this paper, which is a measurement of out-of-band emission of OFDM signal. Nonlinearity of the power amplifier in OFDM transmitter is specially focused on, and the statistical characteristic of out-of-emission is quantitatively expressed by APD spectrum view.

articleTitle: Occurrences of Received Power Anomalous Statistics in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, we present and improve a broadband statistical analysis of anomalous occurrences inside an electromagnetic reverberation chamber. Besides the traditional Anderson-Darling (AD) test, used as a statistical metric for the distance between theoretical and experimental distributions, we introduce the Pearson system, able to assign a distribution family by knowledge of the first two scale invariants, namely skewness and kurtosis. It is shown that such a system can be used as a test to detect departures of idealized statistics for random fields. In particular, while the AD test is sensitive to low part distortions (as opposite to low values of the support) of the DF, i.e., rejects hypothesis, the Pearson category changes whether right tail is far apart. As a particular case, when both the tests flag out a departure, measured distribution is completely different from the asymptotic one. Upon analysis of the received power, it is found that overmoded regime follows a Pearson type I (beta) or type VI (beta prime) distribution, while undermoded and anomalous occurrences follow a Pearson type IV distribution. This corresponds to a right tail departure and is physically explained by the presence of higher-order coherency, recently predicted by theory.

articleTitle: Immunity Modeling of the LM2902 Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Component models that predict functional failure are necessary for predicting the immunity of systems to electromagnetic interference (EMI). A method to extract these models using measurements on integrated circuits (ICs) already exists. This measurement method for ICs with single-ended connections is extended, to include ICs with differential connections. The LM2902 op-amp is measured and modeled as a first case study.

articleTitle: Power Line Impedance Characterization of Automotive Loads at the Power Line Communication Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A complete system able to measure complex impedance, both in magnitude and phase, of an automotive electrical load is designed. The development of such system emerged from the need of measure the impedance of these loads in a wide range of frequencies (100 kHz to 30 MHz) while being connected to power supply and in operation. This powered up condition introduces several problems when the impedance is measured by means of traditional instruments such as Vector Network Analyzers (VNA), which could be damaged by transients. Understanding the behaviour of electrical cars loads in the frequency domain is of primary importance not only for in-vehicle Power Line Communication (PLC) channels response, but also to understand electromagnetic emissions (EMI) problems related with this type of communications.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution from Sector-Configuration Mobile Base Station Antenna System for Human RF Exposure Assessment
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents the electric field distribution from a mobile base station antenna system that is configured with sector radio zones to evaluate human RF exposure. The radiated near field of a vertical dipole linear array antenna is estimated using actual field measurements and the near-field to far-field transform technique. The field power density from the antenna system constructed using six vertical linear array antennas is calculated using a simple linear combination of field power densities from each antenna to determine the compliance boundary of the antenna system for the exposure limit. The results show that the compliance boundary of the e-field for the combined six antennas does not expand significantly compared to that for a single antenna in the direction of the main beam.

articleTitle: Undesired Emission from Magnetic-Resonant Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Undesired emission from magnetic-resonant wireless power transfer is discussed. At first, we investigate resonant mechanism by using MoM simulation. We elucidate that there are odd mode and even mode resonance, which are modeled by two electric dipoles excited in-phase and out-of-phase, respectively. Next, we calculate effective isotropic radiation power (EIRP) for odd and even mode frequencies. We unveiled that the EIRP for even mode is 18dB smaller than odd mode.

articleTitle: Application of Transient Pulses on Power Supply Networks using Commercial off-the-Shelf (CotS) Hardware
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper deals with the development of ultra wide band pulse devices using Commercial off-the-Shelf (CotS) hardware and the propagation of waves on standard power supply cables. The major goal is to create wide band transients and pulses with simple electronic equipment and to achieve high voltages and low pulse rise times. The propagation of these signals on common power lines is examined to analyse and forecast the effects on attached devices.

articleTitle: Definition of APD-Based Emission Limits for the Protection of Coded Wireless Systems from Impulsive Interference
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The definition of emission requirements in terms of amplitude probability distribution (APD) is studied for the protection of digital wireless systems with error correction coding. Focusing on coherent binary phase-shift keying with convolutional coding and Viterbi decoding, a simple approximation of bit error probability (BEP) is derived in terms of the APD for non-Gaussian interferences that can be modeled by Middleton's class A model. By using the BEP expression, discussion is made on how APD-based emission limits can be defined for protecting coded wireless systems from impulsive interferences.

articleTitle: Towards a Global Approach for the Characterization of IC's and on Board Shielding Components
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Due to the impact of higher and higher frequencies, the direct radiated effects of components on a PCB are becoming important. For this reason, an appropriate SE characterisation of small in-circuit enclosures and the accompanying shielding gaskets at frequencies above 1 GHz is needed. Although the standard IEEE Std 1302™ and the standard IEEE Std 299™ are dealing with SE measurements, even up to the higher frequency range, the methods proposed in these standard are not applicable for these type of shielding components. A method overcoming this problem is proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Calculations and Measurements of Input Impedance of Converter Traction Vehicles in Aspect of Interferences Level Reduction
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Modern traction vehicles with static inverters are furnished with input filter. A few input filters of chosen traction vehicles are considered in this paper. The following were calculated: input impedance for load with asynchronous motors, impedance for idle operation. Results obtained from calculations have been compared with measurements conducted on real traction vehicles during normal operation. These impedances were compared with requirements in force in some countries. The authors of the paper think, that obligatory implementation of minimal value of input impedance of vehicle may be a method of decreasing harmonics level generated by traction substation loaded with inverter locomotive.

articleTitle: Measurement Setups to Quantify the Electric Field Strength Inside Shielded Enclosures: Presentation of Different Approaches for an Automated Local Electric Field Strength Scan in the inside of Different Shielded Enclosures
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Automated measurement setups are widely spread in common EMC test labors. This paper shows some approaches of fully automated local scans of the electric field and demonstrates how powerful field scans are. Exemplary results demonstrate the broad spectrum of applications and the impressive results and insights into electromagnetic wave propagation.

articleTitle: Design of Absorber Panels for Oblique Incidence using Wire Array Sheet
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, the design technique of absorber panels for oblique incidence is proposed. The reflection characteristics of the absorber panels show the anisotropy in oblique incidence. By using the wire array sheet, the linearly polarized wave reflection coefficient and the circular polarized wave reflection coefficient in oblique incidence can be matched.

articleTitle: Dimensions of a Dark Spot, Produced by the Compensation Method
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Use of compensation method for creation of weak field area located in an antenna near region is considered. A method of two radiators systems calculation is based on the theory of folded dipoles. The structure is broken down into two substructures: a two-wire long line and a monopole with a stepped variation of equivalent radius. Input impedances and fields of radiators are calculated. Form and dimensions of dark spot and structure parameters provided its maximal dimensions are determined.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Stirring Strategy for the Vibrating Intrinsic Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This work describes the definition, application and assessment of a factorial plan with the aim of gaining insight on what kind of stirring strategy could work the best in a vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber. Three different stirring strategies were defined as factors of a factorial plan. We assess the overall reverberation performance according to three different indicators. With the help of the main effect plots and the interaction plots it is possible to extract general guidelines on how the best stirring process should be.

articleTitle: Broadband Determination of Complex Permittivity and Permeability of High-Loss Materials
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A coaxial-line-based technique is investigated to characterize the complex EM-parameters of high-loss material over a broad frequency band. To simultaneously determine complex permittivity and permeability, two complex reflection coefficients are measured from the material-under-test with two different thicknesses. After a brief discussion of the principle of the proposed technique, uncertainty analysis is conducted to perfect this technique. Uncertainty equations in differential forms are established for the simultaneous measurement of complex electromagnetic (EM) parameters in the systematical consideration of various error factors in measurement. Worst- case differential uncertainty equations were defined while the implicit partial derivation techniques were used to find the coefficients in formulation. Finally, sample materials are measured by the proposed technique from 4 to 16GHz. Good agreement between the measured and reference data validates the effectiveness of our analysis.

articleTitle: Physics-Based Derivation of Design Rules for Vias
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Vias are widely used connections between the different layers of multilayer PCBs. In this paper design rules for signal vias are derived from physics. Analytical formulas for the description of the basic physical effects on a single via are presented. They are used to derive rules for the geometry and the positioning of the via. These design rules are verified using 3d-field simulations.

articleTitle: High Electromagnetic Shielding Effectiveness of Hybrid Glass/Carbon Composite Laminate
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper, the shielding effectiveness of different composite materials is compared. A finite element modeling and measures in a Faraday cage are compared and provide the same level of electromagnetic shielding. Measures have been carried out on different samples from 1 to 6 GHz, providing a highly shielding effectiveness of 80 dB. Furthermore, a surface treatment was performed on these composites to improve the electrical continuity in order to avoid electromagnetic leakage. Moreover several bounding composite has been manufactured in order to compare the level of shielding effectiveness compared to a simple plate. This study has shown the possibility to replace a carbon fibre reinforced composite by a single ply of carbon fibre on each of the external surfaces of a glass fibre reinforced composite for a military application of electromagnetic shielding. This method reduces the cost of materials while providing a high level of electromagnetic shielding.

articleTitle: A Broadband Time-Domain EMI Measurement System for Measurements up to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Using time-domain methods, emission measurements can be accelerated by several orders of magnitude in comparison to measurements with traditional EMI-receivers. In this paper, a novel time-domain EMI measurement system for the frequency range from 9 kHz to 18 GHz is presented. It combines ultra-fast analog-to-digital-conversion and real-time digital signal processing on a field-programmable-gate-array (FPGA) with ultra-broadband multi-stage down-conversion. With a 9 kHz IF-filter, a measurement over the whole frequency range can be performed in around three minutes with highest sensitivity. The results of the noisefloor measurements imply, that the system, with its low noise figure of 6-8 dB, meets the enhanced sensitivity requirements over the whole frequency range up to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of Multilayer Composite Materials for Lightning Problems in Aircraft Applications
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The increased use of composite materials in aeronautic industry and the replacement of metallic elements by CFRP ones had led to the development of specific numerical model to understand their electromagnetic behaviour and to better control the current distributions into structures. The electrical conductivity of composite materials significantly influences the design of protections against lightning direct and indirect effects and the management of functional current return inside an aircraft. This paper presents a numerical modelling of multilayer composites materials in a frequency range comprised between the continuous up to few MHz used to address lightning applications. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Improvement of Russian Regulatory System on Protection against Electromagnetic Attacks
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The article deals with problems of regulatory system development on protection against electromagnetic attacks in Russia. It takes international experience of standards development and peculiarities of Russian regulatory system into consideration.

articleTitle: Effective Method for IEEE 802.11 Hidden Transmission
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper describes a new concept of hidden transmission method for IEEE 802.11 wireless networks. This method is designed especially for use in military applications and uses changing transmission channels and scrambling fragmented data in the MAC layer.

articleTitle: THD Measurement by Multi-Frequency Synchronous Detection
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Multi-frequency synchronous detection allows THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) measurement with the simultaneous presence of the analysed signal and other accompanying signals. These accompanying signals can be noise and/or periodic signal asynchronous to the analysed signal. In this paper, the principles for using of multi-frequency synchronous detection for THD measurement are presented. The influence of the simultaneous presence of the analysed signal and other accompanying signals has been analysed. Example simulations illustrating the above-mentioned considerations have been carried out.

articleTitle: CE Marking of Military Equipment: It is the Law! How to do it?
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Several European Union Members States exempted the implementation of the EMC Directive for defence contracts. According the lawyers, and validated in a court case, this is illegal, and thus the EMC Directive is applicable for military equipment too, except when an exemption for a clearly defined case has been granted. The European Commission confirmed this conclusion in an interpretative communication. The EMC Directive only gives essential requirements. The default route, giving presumption of conformity, is making use of harmonized standards. The alternative route is the use of standards which have not been harmonised. Military standards are not harmonised, and are already in use as the reference in contracts between supplier and customer/user. Using the (test) evidence based on the military standards can therefore be used to prove compliance with the essential requirements of the EMC Directive, making additional testing superfluous. This paper describes the routes to compliance for military equipment.

articleTitle: Narrowband Transmission Quality in Presence of Modified IEEE 802.15.4a UWB Signal
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents results of measurement of narrowband transmission quality in presence of impulse radio UWB interference. In the first part of paper, unmodified IEEE 802.15.4a IR UWB signal is used. Then some modification of transmitted pulse sequence is proposed, which allow to reduce UWB power spectral density at frequency of narrowband transmission. Finally narrowband transmission quality in presence of modified ultrawideband interference signal is presented.

articleTitle: Ergonomically Realistic Assessment of Hazards Related to Electromagnetic Fields Exposure While the use of Welding Devices
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper presents realistic and standardized approach to modeling the electromagnetic hazards from gun resistant welding devices. Numerical calculations of induced current densities and internal electric field were carried out with the use of 5. and 95. centile workers body models. Investigations concerned both realistic workers posture and postures of geometries A, B and C stated in EN 50505:2007. The results shown that standardized geometries of exposure scenarios recommended by EN 50505:2007 standard may not cover the worst case of worker’s exposure to magnetic field from gun welding device (representing by induced current density and internal E-field).

articleTitle: Evaluation of the LCLs of Metallic Cables in Customer Premises and Immunity of VDSL Systems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes a number of tests of the longitudinal conversion loss (LCL) of metallic cables and the immunity of VDSL systems. The LCL of metallic cables depends on the structures and configurations of the cables. In previous studies based on ITU-T recommendations, the metallic cables used for the measurement of LCL and immunity were set up on the ground reference plane. However, in practice, metallic cables in customer premises are rarely laid on the ground plane or near metal materials. In this paper, the LCL of metallic cables and the immunity levels for VDSL systems related to different cable structures (single-layer, twisted-pair, and star-quad cables) and different cable configurations (straight, folded, and coiled) have been evaluated for various distances between the metallic cable and the ground reference plane.

articleTitle: Partial Vacuum Formation in Short Gap and Effect on Discharge Parameters
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Fast electrode moving speed results in partial vacuum state at short gap, and generates transition phenomenon between avalanche process and surface process in short gap discharge. Property forming partial vacuum is analyzed, and explanation was given on the influence on discharge parameters from partial vacuum formation.

articleTitle: International Telecommunication Union
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010

articleTitle: K-Factor as an Accurate Estimator of the Stirring Efficiency in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper aims to improve the characterization of the electromagnetic environment in a mode-stirred reverberation chamber. The ideal Rayleigh distribution of a rectangular component of the electric field requires that all the propagating paths are well stirred. That means that no unstirred energy remains during the stirring process. This work focus on a meticulous analysis of the Rician K-factor as a potential estimate of the quality of the reverberating environment. A comparison with high power goodness-of-fit tests results show that estimating K should be highly recommended for evaluating the accuracy of the mode stirring process.

articleTitle: Modeling of Bulk Current Injection (BCI) Setups for Virtual Automotive IC Tests
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The Bulk Current Injection (BCI) method is widely used for RF immunity testing of automotive systems and ICs in electronics industry. During testing detected IC failures may lead to expensive redesigns and cause seriously delays of a product launch. To evaluate the chip immunity in early design stages it is desired to perform virtual tests based on accurate models. In this paper an accurate and fast to simulate behavioural model of a BCI injection clamp is presented. The applicability is shown with an RF immunity investigation of a sample DUT. Several different configurations of the BCI test setup with different wire lengths and application-dependent line terminations are analyzed. Specific attention is paid to test setup configurations where supply and ground cables are subject of injection. The common and differential mode disturbances and PCB ground shifts are measured and modeled. The simulations show good correlation to measurements and allow performing RF immunity investigations of the designed DUTs on earlier design stages.

articleTitle: Simulation of Thin Conductive Panels using Digital Filters in Transmission-Line Modelling
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes the time-domain simulation of electromagnetic wave interaction with thin conductive panels using the Transmission-Line Modelling (TLM) method. The approach is based on digital filtering techniques and allows the incorporation of thin lossy panels into simulations without the need to explicitly mesh the panel. Validation results are shown and it is demonstrated that the technique leads to a very substantial reduction in computational effort.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Comtest 5 × 4 × 3 m3 Reverberating Chamber
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A 5×4 m reverberating chamber of 3 m height has recently been installed in the group EES at Eindhoven University of Technology. The room is intended for EMC studies of emission and immunity of equipment and for the coupling of installation cables and shielding structures. Initially the room will be used up to 1 GHz; the final goal is 40 GHz. The lowest usable frequency depends on the room size. The quality factor and the electrical field strength related to the input power have been modeled to predict the chambers behavior. Model and the measurements match acceptably well. A simulation has been preformed as well with a Method of Moments model (FEKO) and indicates that the room fulfills the IEC requirements (less than 4 - 3 dB standard deviation) on statistical field uniformity starting at 200 MHz. Higher frequencies up to 1 GHz have been calculated as well, and agreement with IEC has been observed. The calibration results were not in line with the models and simulation. The models, simulations and an investigation of the calibration results have proved that the calibration contains errors. Comtest is writing new software to correct these errors to recalibrate the room in the near future.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference in Complex Power Supply Networks
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The power supply electromagnetic interference (EMI) phenomena are strongly related to power quality (PQ). Power quality is conventionally related to the quality of supply in terms of fast voltage variations (sags, surges), slow variations (flicker) and harmonics. The majority of these fluctuations are caused by variations in the load. In modern dense distribution networks with a large number of generators and many fast switching consumers, the risk of electromagnetic interference is increasing. A comparison of standards describing EMI phenomena, including the PQ issues, is made. The risk of electromagnetic interference, including due to transient effects, via the power distribution network will be estimated using transmission lines for the network and behavioral models for non-linear generators and connected equipment.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Analysis of Shielding Effectiveness of Lightning Protection Systems in the Case of Nearby Strike
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A numerical analysis of shielding effectiveness of grid-like spatial shields in the frequency domain is presented for the case of a nearby lightning strike. Attenuation characteristics for electric and magnetic fields of different lightning protection systems (LPS) are investigated. Dissimilarities between shielding effectiveness for electric and magnetic fields are presented. The shielding effectiveness frequency band depends on building dimensions and is not the same for both types of fields.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Propagation Channel-Measurements and Simulations in Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The coverage area and reliability of wireless applications in industrial environments can be limited by electromagnetic interference and other noise. The use of ultrawideband (UWB) communication systems can be effective in these environments because it affords advantages such as multiple access, lack of significant multipath fading and potentially easier penetrability through various materials. The characterization of the signal propagation mechanism of UWB channels is important from the viewpoint of radio systems design and system performance analysis. In this paper, the results of UWB measurements and simulations in line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) industrial multipath environments for three frequency bands are presented.

articleTitle: Multipole Parameters Out of Measurements: Uncertainty Considerations
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A measurement method for a multipole approximation of arbitrary electromagnetic sources is motivated and described. In order to analyze the influences of different error sources, a method for the comparison of radiation patterns is introduced and the one dimensional correlation coefficient is identified as a quality factor for the similarity of radiation patterns. The quality factor is used for the analysis of different sources of errors, which can occur in measurements. The paper shows, that one of the main influences on multipole approximations are reflections.

articleTitle: A Study of Stochasticity Effects of Cable Bundles in Automotive EMC Problems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this study the simulation method is developed to account for stochasticity effects in multi-cable bundles. When dealing with automotive electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) on embedded electronics, propagation of disturbing signals along wires has a great impact, especially on radiated emission. Cable bundles in automobiles are mostly stochastic and require specific analysis for EM/EMC behavior. Developed simulation model for the stochastic multi-cable bundles is based on lumped circuit model of the multi transmission lines with randomly formed cross-sections along cable system. Interaction of cables with surrounding environment is simulated using hybridization of transmission line theory with the Method of Moments. Validation of developed approach is performed against measurements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Methods for the Summation of Log-Normal Distributions
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: When carrying out coverage predictions for RF signals, statistics play a big part and the statistical nature of the predicted values cannot be ignored. In the particular case of location variation, the signals are assumed to follow a log-normal distribution and various methods are available for carrying out summations of such signals. This article examines the different algorithms in an attempt to assess the suitability of each one and to identify the optimum method to use. Two main scenarios are considered. The first one deals with the summation of a series of signals with various mean values, such as might be used when summing the contributions of a number of interferers. The second one deals with the best solution to minimize mean and standard deviation error of the sum. In both cases, the impact of the mean level and standard deviation of the contributors is considered.

articleTitle: Proposal of Radiated Emission Measurement using VHF-LISN
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: VCCI Council Technical Sub-committee has investigated the differences of radiated emission measurement results [1] - [5]. It was confirmed that one of the main cause of the dispersion of radiated emission measurement results was the difference of the power line-to-ground impedance of the power supply for the equipment under test (EUT). For the improvement of the dispersion, VCCI Council manufactured the experimental VHF-LISN (Very High Frequency - Line Impedance Stabilization Network). And VCCI Council confirmed the validity of this VHF-LISN.

articleTitle: The Use of Corrugations to Enhance Shielding Effectiveness of Fiber Optic Waveguide Feedthrough
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: In this paper we show by practical measurements that the shielding effectiveness for a circular waveguide feedthrough is much lower for high frequencies when it is filled with fiber optic cables compared to when it is empty. The reason for this is discussed and a method for improving the attenuation at high frequencies when the feedthrough is filled with fiber optic cables is presented. The introduced wave trap consists of cascaded corrugations with different dimensions. It could easily be manufactured as a separate unit that can be mounted on existing feedthroughs without having any negative effect in terms of the capability of handling fiber optic cables. The theory behind the wave trap is explained and numerical simulations as well as measurement results are presented in order to prove the function.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modelling of Large Scale Structures with Non Linear Devices
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The introduction of new materials in large structures as aircrafts has considerably changed the qualification of systems. In particular, electrical systems have to be robust in a more severe environment than for metallic airplanes. This is mainly due to the presence of composite materials inside the structure. This paper deals with EMC inside the system and presents a methodology to take into account the structure effects and equipment modelling. The originality is to perform frequency domain simulation for 3D structure, approximations of the frequency domain responses with hybrid code or vector fitting techniques and solve the full system with non linear device in the time domain.

articleTitle: 105m Long Anechoic Chamber for High Power Microwave Measurements
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The Gramat Research Centre possesses a large building 105 metres in length. Previously used for a completely different purpose, the decision was taken to rehabilitate this facility as a RF shielded anechoic chamber of large dimensions.

articleTitle: Statistical Properties of Electromagnetic Environment in Wireless Networks, Intra-Network Electromagnetic Compatibility and Safety
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Statistical properties of electromagnetic environment in wireless networks affecting its intra-network electromagnetic compatibility and safety are studied. The analysis is based on the standard propagation channel model, a Poisson model of random spatial distribution of transmitters, and a threshold-based model of the victim receptor behaviour (radio receiver or human body). The distribution of dominant interference level is derived and analysed under various network and system configurations. The aggregate interference is dominated by the nearest transmitter one. The distribution of the unordered single-node interference is independent of the transmitters’ power and their spatial density and is the same for homogeneous and non-homogeneous networks. The outage probability is used as a measure of not only the wireless link quality-of-service, but also of environmental risks induced by electromagnetic radiation. The maximum acceptable interference levels for reliable link performance and for low environmental risks are surprisingly similar.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multiconductor Transmission Line's Sensitivity to Damage : Two Complementary Approaches
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: As electronic devices are more and more used in many different fields, monitoring the health and the ageing of complex wiring networks becomes a crucial need. Although experimental methods, such as Reflectometry can quite accurately localize hard defects (e.g.: open or short circuits), none is currently able to detect and study their evolution from their emergence (soft defects). This article proposes two complementary ways to answer this issue. The first one relies on analytical results whereas the other is based on simulations. Each one has its own benefits but using them in synergy could be an easy and promising way of assessing the ageing of cables.

articleTitle: Quantifying TEM Cell Electric and Magnetic Field Coupling to Arbitrary Orientation of Microstrip Lines
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) analysis of high-speed circuits is becoming mandatory due to the rapid increase in operating frequencies, RF interference and layout densities. Radiated susceptibility tests are important part of overall EMC analysis. In this paper the focus of investigation is on models of the coupling between a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) field generated by the TEM cell and the arbitrarily oriented microstrip lines. The Method of Lines (MoL) is used to calculate the capacitance matrix for microstrip lines having different widths. This capacitance matrix is used for calculation of inductance matrix, i.e. self and mutual inductances. The calculated values of mutual capacitances and mutual inductances are introduced in coupling models for arbitrarily oriented lines, and simulation results are compared against measurement results. The presented models are very accurate and include only passive elements, and therefore can be used for efficient coupling modelling between microstrip lines and the TEM cell septum.

articleTitle: Determination of Acceptable Levels of Noise in Power-Line Communications
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Noise-immunity of remote control systems for electrical energy converters which use power lines to transmit control signals was considered. Influence of SNR (signal to noise ratio) and bit rate on noise-immunity was explored.

articleTitle: A Immunity Measurement Bench Dedicated to Analog to Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents the design of a measurement bench dedicated to Analog To Digital Converter immunity. The immunity of the circuit is modeled and the ADC circuit exhibits susceptibility for voltage disturbances. The bench is presented and it uses a DPI derived technique in order to inject a disturbance voltage. A criterion study is done and some immunity results are given. At the end, the improvement of the measurement technique is described.

articleTitle: RFID Systems in Medical Environment: EMC Issues
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: RFID is a promising technology in the healthcare area in order to improve patient safety and increase efficiency and reduce costs in the daily healthcare work. This paper analyzes the available literature regarding both interference of RFID systems in medical equipment and the interferences of medical equipment on RFID systems. The conclusion of this analysis is that is necessary to develop standards in order to protect medical equipment from RFID interferences and standards to plan the deployment of RFID installations taking into account electromagnetic compatibility issues.

articleTitle: Pacemaker Interference by Low Frequency Electric and Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents the results of the interference of pacemakers by low frequency electric and magnetic fields in comparison to the actual standards. The assessment of the interference especially for pacemakers on the basis of standards is very restrictive. For this reason the actual standards are discussed and probabilities for a detailed assessment submitted. Based on the coupling mechanism in the low frequency range for electric and magnetic fields the resulting induced voltages at the entrance of the pacemaker were calculated. For this analytical solutions are compared with measurements and numerical models. In the context of this study a program for the employer's liability insurance association for energy, textile, electro, media products was developed. This program provides an assessment for a detailed analysis of the pacemaker disturbances.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of UHF RFID System Susceptibility to in-Channel Radio Interference
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The effects of in-channel electromagnetic interference (EMI) on the behavior and performance of a modern ultra high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) system are here investigated and assessed. In particular, meaningful results from experiments are summarized and commented with the aim of highlighting the importance of EMI issues in the design and setup of UHF RFID systems. Experiments have been conducted on a suitably arranged testbed configured in such a way as to emulate a typical identification process of items within a given volume. The testbed includes a real-life UHF RFID reader and a set of EPCglobal Gen-2 Class-1 tags. Measurements are accomplished in terms of system efficiency, intended as percentage of correctly identified tags.

articleTitle: Lightning protection strategy used in LOFAR radio telescope
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: One of the anticipated threats for world's largest radio telescope with the acronym LOFAR is lightning. The synthesis telescope exists of at least 36 stations in The Netherlands and 8 European stations with a total antenna area of 0.29 km<sup>2</sup>. The risk area is about 0.6 km<sup>2</sup> resulting in at least 1 hit every year assuming a typical lightning density of 2 km<sup>-2</sup> y<sup>-1</sup>. Cost-effective protection measures have been taken at printed circuit board (PCB) level of antennas and receivers that are connected by up to 100 m of underground coaxial cables, using conventional lightning protection electronics. We expect that individual antennas are only damaged when a lightning stroke impacts within four meters distance. The estimated induced currents, voltages and charges using simplified electro magnetic modeling indicate that the protection measures avoid induction damage to the cables and connected receivers.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Radiated Emissions from Adjustable Speed Drives
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The analysis of a complex system, such as a power converter combined with a motor is difficult. The compliance with the limit values for emission and immunity which are defined for variable-speed drives in the product norm EN 618003 has to be guaranteed by evaluations, measurements or simulations. The development of tools and methods to achieve electromagnetic compatibility for variable-speed drive systems was the aim of the described investigations. The manufacturers of power drive systems should be enabled to qualify the EMC of their systems during development process by using these tools. The main focus of the paper lies on the prediction of the electromagnetic emission of the system.

articleTitle: Modeling Conducted EMI of Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper presents a model for electromagnetic interferences (EMI) of a matrix converter (MC). The model is based on a high frequency equivalent circuit and a calculation, using a combined time and frequency domain approach and following the sequence: “EMI source identifications → propagation path impedances → derived disturbance”. In this method, different equivalent circuits have to be used to study the common mode (CM) and the differential mode (DM) conducted EMI, both to the supply side and to the load side. The advantages of the proposed procedure are the computational time reduction and the lack of convergence problems, which arise when using pure time domain methods. The paper is focused on the application of the method to common mode (CM) EMI calculation of a matrix converter. The simulation results of this work will permit the calculation of currents which leak through the ground path.

articleTitle: Technical Aspects of EMF Monitoring in the Environment
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The work presents the technical aspects of the assessment of exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF) in the environment. In the paper are presented the parameters of the EMF important to the biosphere exposure, presented methods for the EMF assessing: theoretical analysis of EMF intensity in the proximity of EMF sources and also the measurements in situ. Review of measurement methods and identification of limitations of the measuring devices and estimation of the expected EMF intensity in the municipal environment and environmental measurements uncertainty are presented.

articleTitle: Implementation of ITU GE06 Agreement for Digital Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010

articleTitle: Field Coupling to Randomly-Routed Wires: Theoretical and Experimental Comparison
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The coupling of electromagnetic field to randomly-routed wires is studied in this article. Random wires’ configurations are generated through a stochastic model and estimations of the output currents are based on Transmission Lines Theory. Several random configurations are manually reproduced with a copper wire and used for measurements in a GTEM cell and a Fully Anechoic Chamber. Comparisons between theoretical and experimental results are provided. Statistical behaviors of the randomly-routed wires according to the incident field polarization angle are shown. Likewise, a fast method to estimate the wires statistical parameters and maximum interference values is presented.

articleTitle: Nearfield-Immunity Scan on Printed Circuit Board Level with Suitable Calibration Method
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A new immunity scan method is presented for assessing the sensitivity of circuits in close proximity to the nearfield of noise emission sources. The measurement setup primarily consists of a positioning robot with a small field probe, fed by a signal source and a power amplifier. A suitable calibration method to adjust the interference field strength is suggested. The method is verified by calculations and measurements of the coupling into a transmission line. As an application example, the bit-error-ratio of a binary signal transmission is evaluated, depending on the interference field amplitude and the frequency.

articleTitle: Deployment of DVB-H Networks in Urban Areas using Cable TV Networks
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The paper presents the concept of using a cable TV (CATV) network as a signal distribution network for dense DVB-H SFN networks with low-power transmitters in urban areas. The results of signal quality tests are also presented as well as the results of propagation tests in the urban environment. The proposed solution is competitive with traditional DVB-H networks thanks to the time of network development, better indoor coverage and costs.

articleTitle: Magnetic Shielding Effectiveness of Multilayer Wire Mesh Screen
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Recently the use of wire mesh screens for shielding structure especially for medical diagnostic applications as MRI, is a very active field of research and industrial development, due to their light-weight structures and capability which allow both light and air transmission. To improve a magnetic field shielding a simple physical model of multilayer shields containing both conductive brass wire mesh screen and magnetic steel SAE sheet, was made and described wiht a simple theoretical model. The effect of air-gap in the adjacent sheet of the multilayer screen, were analyzed with our model and compared with experimental shielding effectiveness measurements. Experimental data shown a quite agreement with the analytical model highlight as useful in shielding against magnetic field for is a wide range of frequencies, the combined effectiveness of magnetic screen, wire-mesh screen and air-gap thickness.

articleTitle: Time Domain Measurements for CISPR 16-1-1 EMI Testing: Novel Method to Trace Interfering RF Disturbances
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Time Domain Measurements are ideal to trace transient and time limited disturbing RF signals. Modern automotive electronic modules are emitting in some cases strong transient RF disturbances. Such signals are getting critical because comfort options like blue tooth connection, external devices with complex integrated RF functionality (automotive WLAN, UMTS, GSM, WCDMA, MIMO devices, multiband smart phones, Net-books) have to interface with integrated car entertainment and control systems. Due to the technical concept of such wireless communication networks with digital modulation schemes, the interferences are often short events with transient characteristics. The use of WLAN and other wireless services in the area of home applications are a further area of interest. Some home appliances are able to interfere with the wireless communication and need further investigation. Especially critical are disturbances with are not continuous, but connected to the operation mode of the home appliance. To capture such RF signals and to perform reproducible measurements is difficult. Today such measurements are possible using Time Domain Measurement Systems. Those units are equipped with very fast A/D converters, digital filters and calculate in parallel several thousand frequency points using the Fourier analysis.

articleTitle: Implementation of Cognitive Radio in Seamcat
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: This paper describes some of the proposed new development of the SEAMCAT software. In particular, the detailed description of the implementation of cognitive radio feature enabling spectrum sensing is presented.

articleTitle: Effects of a Radiated Emission Test Site on a Receiving Antenna Scattering Parameters
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The effects of a radiated emission test site on the scattering parameters of a measurement antenna are here investigated. To the purpose, experiments are conducted measuring the input impedance of a reference loop antenna in different test sites and varying the antenna position from the ground floor. The purpose is to investigate how the site characteristics may influence the antenna scattering parameters and consequently the accuracy in electric field measurements. The analysis is finally extended to the case of a standard 30-200 MHz biconical antenna.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Disturbance on the Ethernet Ports of Telecommunication Equipments in Customer Premises
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Recently both video and high-quality voice services have been provided by using Ethernet cables to connect telecommunication equipment with a set-top box (STB) or other IP-based communication device. As such services require low delays and a low frame error rate, any electromagnetic disturbance may strongly affect user satisfaction. Therefore, it is important to immunize the telecommunication equipment on customer premises against such signal interference. However, the required level of immunity for internal communication ports on telecommunication equipment, including Ethernet ports, has not been clarified. In this paper, we examine the entry of electromagnetic disturbances via the Ethernet ports of telecommunication equipment on customer premises. We found that electromagnetic disturbances in the 0.15 to 80 MHz range, which occur in AC power supply lines, may be attenuated by a few dB when transmitted through IP-based communication devices such as PCs, HUBs, and STBs, and may enter the Ethernet ports of telecommunication equipment at almost the same level as it appeared in AC power supply lines. Hence we should plan for disturbing waves at Ethernet ports that are as large as those in AC power lines when the immunity requirements for Ethernet ports are considered.

articleTitle: Towards Realistic Test Levels for Bulk Current Injection up to 6 GHz
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: Due to the increasing clock frequencies and decreasing rise times, the mandatory upper frequency limit for radiated emission and susceptibility testing on electronic modules are increasing up to 3 or even 6 GHz. The Bulk Current Injection test method has widely gained acceptance as alternative immunity test method. Unfortunately, test levels for this test method are only available up to 400 MHz. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a theoretical model based on antenna reciprocity that can be used to predict the worst-case current that is induced into a typical Bulk Current Injection set-up by an incoming plane wave.

articleTitle: Importance Analysis to Describe Reliability of Systems
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: The complexity of modern systems on the one hand and the rising threat of (intentional) EMI on the other hand increase the necessity of systematical reliability assessment for electronic devices. For that purpose, methods known from probabilistic risk analysis offer convenient and proven approaches. Complex systems are composed of modules and subsystem which can lead to a failure, breakdown or even damage of the entire system when it is exposed to EMI. Generally, not every module or subsystem reacts equally to EMI. Moreover, consequences for the entire system caused by a failure of different subsystems may differ. Consequently, it is essential to determine those subsystems which contribute most to the failure probability of the entire system. An appropriate instrument to determine this contribution is the importance analysis which is presented in this paper. With the help of importance analysis best candidates for improvement efforts can be identified. Furthermore, the classical importance analysis is extended in order to include also the physical quantities such as pulse amplitude or shielding.

articleTitle: “Virtual Testing Area” for Solving EMC Problems of Spatially Distributed Radiosystems based on Automated Double-Frequency Test System
publicationTitle: 9th International Symposium on EMC Joint with 20th International Wroclaw Symposium on EMC, EMC Europe 2010
abstract: A new technology named as “Virtual Testing Area” and intended for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) analysis in complexes of radio systems is presented. This technology is based on semi-physical EMC modeling with an expedient ratio of mathematical and physical modeling of (a) electromagnetic environment (EME) and (b) behavior of radio receivers in complicated EME. The proposed technology has the following advantages: (a) high informativity of the Automated double-frequency testing technique (ADFTT), which is used for characterization of receivers, (b) high efficiency of the Discrete nonlinear analysis (DNA) technique, which is used for behavior simulation of receivers, (c) high objectivity of EME modeling with the use of digital area maps and geoinformation systems (GIS), (d) efficiency and low cost of software-controlled physical modeling of receivers in laboratory conditions by using the equipment of Automated Double-Frequency Test System (ADFTS).
